title: Define settlement correction, reversal uniqueness, and control-account projections
description:
References: §§5.6/5.7, 8.1/8.2, Appendix A/B/F (lines 419-423, 519-522, 536, 1165, 1241-1246, 1335, 1339).
Open amount = original minus summed SETTLES, but no immutable application-undo law is specified when a receipt or invoice is reversed/replaced. Reversing a settled receipt's GL legs leaves the invoice closed unless settlement effects reverse too; copying the original settles into the reversal can double-apply. Define versioned application effects and their bitemporal fold, target-side/unit validation, and over-application protection.
Acyclic SUPERSEDES plus exact target negation does not prevent two different idempotency keys from reversing/replacing one original twice. O + (-O) + (-O) is still acyclic and each reversal satisfies the local rule. Specify which reversal/replacement lifecycle actions are permitted and the concurrency witness; reversing a reversal must remain explicit if supported.
§5.6 says native detail postings inherently fold into the control account. The Register key schema has one account_ref, while only Leaf accounts accept legs. Define summary roll-up ownership, prohibit double counting and specify the externally fed detail-vs-summary representation so there is no second posting universe.
Acceptance: receipt applied then reversed; invoice replaced after partial application; concurrent duplicate reversals; two customers under an AR control account plus external-summary import. W2/W3, G0/G2.
notes: Addressed in ff3b6eb: §5.7 application effects versioned (open = original - SETTLES + UNSETTLES; reversals carry kernel-emitted unsettles; replacements re-declare, never copy); §8.2 reversal/replacement uniqueness by identity-derived vids (second reversal = AlreadyLive conflict; reversing a reversal explicit); §5.6 leaf-only register cells with rollup cells for summaries and external detail outside the book. FA-INV-08 clauses unsettle, reversed-once. Left open for re-review.

title: Remove the ungated full-byte document read (`Book::read_document`) that bypasses the privileged-caveat gate
description:
WHY: plan §9.6 interim posture: "privileged document bytes are stored in a separate PrivilegedDocument vertex class whose reads require the privileged caveat, evaluated by Steward before query construction — never as a result filter." fa-txf part C2 (88f4d46) implemented a gated `Book::read_document_for(capability, oid)` (crates/fa/src/book.rs:958) that derives redacted views, but the facade also exposes `pub fn read_document(&self, oid)` (book.rs:982) which calls `fa_journal::fetch_document` (crates/fa-journal/src/evidence.rs:783) with no capability and returns the full canonical bytes of any document, privileged or not. Any embedding caller (and any future surface wired to it) bypasses the redaction contract.

WHAT: make the ungated path unreachable from the facade: either remove `read_document` (callers migrate to `read_document_for` with the embedded-owner capability, which must hold `privileged` to see privileged bytes) or make it `pub(crate)` for verification-only internals with a doc comment stating why; audit every caller of `fetch_document` (`rg -n fetch_document crates`) so each sits behind an admission check or is a verify-only path that never returns bytes to a caller; add a topology/grep gate in check.sh that fails if a public facade fn returns `Document` bytes without a `Capability` parameter.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: owner posture with `privileged` reads full bytes via read_document_for; [ ] planted negative: a non-privileged capability receives only the redacted view; a compile-fail or gate test proves no public ungated byte path exists; [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-10.core for documents); [ ] consumers: fa-txf, fa-6l9 productions, fa-7dw; [ ] no-claim boundary: protects bytes at the facade; storage-level access to the book directory is outside this boundary (book keys).

title: fa-sim-harness: lab runtime (asupersync lab + substrate lab VFS) with registered crash points at every pipeline barrier, seeded scheduling, DPOR over post-vs-close and the other registered races, crashpacks with replay commands, in-sim consistency oracles; Genesis campaign green under lab (G1)
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-10, CobaltGull): "Simulation-first (fa-sim)" is a design pillar (AGENTS.md verification ladder; plan §16) and Gate G1 requires the Genesis slice "green under lab and live". At 96d1918 there is no lab harness at all: no fa-sim-harness crate (W1 names it), no crash points, no DPOR, no crashpacks, no replay command; the only concurrency test is the policy-epoch race. The post-vs-close race that the doctrine calls "an SSI conflict, never a cron job's finding" is untested in either order. Every later workstream accrues its scenario campaigns onto this harness, so it is on the critical path to G1.

WHAT:
1. `crates/fa-sim-harness` (verification layer, test-only consumers): wraps asupersync's lab runtime (virtual time, seeded scheduling) and the substrate's lab VFS (torn writes, bit flips, ENOSPC, fsync lies) behind one `Lab { seed, schedule, vfs_faults }`; the facade `fa::Book` opens under it through the existing `Entropy::deterministic` and a lab `PurposeContexts` (no new API on Book that production code could reach).
2. Crash points at every pipeline barrier the kernel already has (admission, witnesses read, legs staged, mirrors moved, commit): a registered `CrashPoint` enum, each named in a `registries/crash_points.toml` row with the invariant it guards; the harness kills at each point and reopens; FA-INV-04/14/16 oracles (register-equals-fold, accumulator consistency, mirror-equals-payload) run after every reopen.
3. DPOR over post-vs-close, concurrent application, promotion-vs-trunk (when drafts exist), restatement-vs-reopen (when cases exist), sweep-vs-manual-void (fa-ctf): both orders explored; the winner is decided by first-committer-wins over witnesses, never by wall time.
4. Crashpacks: every failing seed writes `<scratch>/crashpacks/<seed>/` with the schedule, the VFS fault log and the exact `cargo test` replay command; the harness prints it; replay is byte-deterministic.
5. Consistency oracles as reusable in-sim checks: balance law, register-equals-fold, subledger-equals-control, admissibility at commit, SoD on approvals, idempotency stability, supersession acyclicity, accumulator consistency, bitemporal monotonicity, projection-equals-payload, erasure leaves amounts intact (those whose subsystems exist run; the rest are registered dormant with the activating bead).
6. Genesis campaign: the existing genesis/differential histories executed under the lab with 1,000 seeds and the full crash matrix; this is the G1 "green under lab" evidence.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: `cargo test -p fa-sim-harness genesis_campaign` runs the matrix green and prints the seed count and crash-point coverage (every registered point hit ≥ 10 times); post-vs-close DPOR explores both orders and each ends in exactly one committed winner; [ ] planted negatives: a harness mutation that skips mirror moves on reopen fails register-equals-fold; a VFS torn-write at the commit barrier with the oracle disabled is caught by the accumulator-consistency check; [ ] proof class: bounded_model (the matrix states its bounds: seeds, depth, fault classes); [ ] consumers: Gate G1, every later campaign, fa-ctf interleavings, fa-s7x promotion races; [ ] no-claim boundary: a green campaign is bounded evidence, never a proof of crash safety beyond the registered points and seeds.

TESTS: the harness has its own unit tests for determinism (same seed → same transcript) and for crashpack replay; campaign logs record seed, point, oracle verdicts; run through rch like every other test.

title: Read-path authorization: every read verb takes a capability evaluated before query construction, with account/period/entity/known_at caveats and whole-entry visibility (doctrine 8, FA-INV-10.whole-entry)
description:
WHY: doctrine 8 — "Capability caveats are enforced before any storage observation … by refusal before query construction. Never as a result filter." At e606b46 balance/trial-balance/explain reads take no capability at all (crates/fa/src/book.rs:1162-1212); `entries_at`/`report_at` fold the whole book (crates/fa-registers/src/lib.rs:228-252, :910). The plan's Auditor (`known_at ≤ seq`), Regulator (scoped, time-boxed), and Production profiles, and the `accounts ⊆ subtree`, `periods`, `entities`, `dimensions` caveats are therefore unexpressible for reads. Separately, an Agent-profile capability is refused on document reads because the read is built with `trunk: true` and trips the trunk-write rule (crates/fa-journal/src/redaction.rs:548, crates/fa-policy/src/admit.rs:39) — reads and writes must be distinct admission classes.

WHAT:
1. fa-policy: `admit_read(capability, ReadScope { verb, coordinate, accounts?, periods?, entities? })` evaluated before any snapshot read; refusal FA-REF code naming the blocking caveat (catalog row); read admission never applies the trunk-write rule.
2. Facade/CLI/fad/MCP: every read verb (tb, explain balance, open-items, entry show, verify *, document read, checkpoint verify, registers materialize's read half) takes the session capability (fa-r3q) or the embedded-owner capability.
3. Whole-entry visibility (§14.2): an entry is observable iff every leg's account and dimensions are in scope; folds over in-scope accounts include in-scope legs of partially visible entries; `explain balance` marks `partially_visible` only under `partial_view`; certificates (fa-cqk) name the capability commitment; a partial fold is never labelled whole-book.
4. known_at caveat: an Auditor pinned `known_at ≤ s` cannot select a later coordinate (refusal), and historical selectors never resurrect revoked authority.
5. fa-reference: visibility model; differential on generated scopes.

ACCEPTANCE:
[ ] positive: an Auditor token pinned at seq s reads tb at s and is refused at head; an account-subtree token's tb contains only that subtree and its certificate names the scope;
[ ] planted negatives: a read whose scope excludes an account the request names → refused before any snapshot read (proven by a counting probe: zero substrate reads on refusal); a partially visible entry without partial_view is not listed; an Agent token reading a document succeeds (regression for the trunk-write misfire);
[ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-10.whole-entry live) + differential;
[ ] consumers: fa-7dw, fa-zgn (engagements), fa-9ae certificates, examiners;
[ ] no-claim boundary: authorization of reads is enforced in FrankenAccounting before query construction (R-WARDEN interim), not by substrate predicate compilation.

TESTS: fa-policy unit; fa-journal/fa-registers kernel tests with a substrate read counter; CLI binary tests per verb; differential with seeds logged.

description:

title: fa-mcp containment: never accept `as`/`grant`/`yes`/`keys` from tool arguments; bind the server's principal and Agent-profile capability at launch; stop the self-approval detector coaching impersonation
description:
WHY: verified at e606b46 — fa-mcp turns agent-supplied tool arguments into fa argv including `--as <principal>`, `--grant <op>`, `--yes` and `--keys <path>` (crates/fa-mcp/src/registry.rs:1381-1388; global flags validated as exposed at :353; unit test :1775-1800 asserts `{"grant":"post_closed","yes":true}` becomes `--grant post_closed --yes`). Every fa-cli handler then self-issues a Human capability for that principal and those ops (`Capability::embedded`, crates/fa-policy/src/capability.rs:237-247). So the MCP surface — the surface built for AI agents — gives an agent full Human authority, lets it choose its identity per call (defeating segregation of duties: plan as `operator`, approve as `controller`), and lets it bypass dangerous-operation gating by passing `yes: true`. The self-approval detector (crates/fa-mcp/src/detect.rs:478-492) answers a detected self-approval with "call fa_time_approve with `as` set to a different, admissible principal" plus a suggested tool call `{"as": "<another principal>"}`: the exact impersonation the plan's §14.3/§14.4 forbid. This is the cheapest high-value fix in the reality check and can land before the full issuance model (fa-v62/fa-r3q).

WHAT:
1. Server launch configuration (CLI args of the fa-mcp binary, never tool arguments): `--book <dir>`, `--keys <file>`, `--principal <name>`, `--profile agent|preparer` (default `agent`), optional `--grant <op>` list bounded by the profile (an Agent profile cannot hold approve/close/reopen/restate/post_closed/migrate/witness/issue_capability/erase). Until fa-v62 lands, the server self-issues exactly one capability at launch from this config and labels every response `authority: {posture: "mcp-launch-config", principal, profile, ops}`.
2. Tool schemas: remove `as`, `grant`, `yes`, `keys` and `book` overrides from every tool's input schema; the argument normalizer refuses them if present with a structured error `{type: "forbidden_argument", data: {fix_hint: "identity and authority are fixed when the server starts; ask the operator to start a server with the profile you need", argument}}` (never silently ignores them).
3. Dangerous operations through MCP require a `confirm_plan` certificate once fa-we7 lands; until then they are refused through MCP with the safe alternative (`--dry-run`/plan file for lock/reopen) — an agent never confirms its own dangerous op with `yes`.
4. Self-approval detector: the fix text names the policy row and says a second, independent approver (a human or a separately launched approver session holding approve) must approve; the suggested tool call is removed. Same audit for every other detector's fix text (`grep -n '"as"' crates/fa-mcp/src`).
5. verbs.toml `[mcp]` rows and the robot-schema pin updated; parity tests updated deliberately (show the before/after diff in the commit message).
6. `fa capabilities --json` and the MCP `robot_docs`/server instructions state the actual binding posture.

ACCEPTANCE:
[ ] positive: an fa-mcp e2e (stdio) session launched with `--profile agent --principal agent-7` can call read tools and `post` on a draft-less book and receives FA-REF-013 (Agent-on-trunk) with the drafts pointer — proving the Agent profile now reaches the kernel from a real surface;
[ ] planted negatives (each reaches exactly one check): a tool call carrying `as` → forbidden_argument; carrying `grant` → forbidden_argument; carrying `yes` → forbidden_argument; a server launched `--profile agent --grant approve` refuses to start with the profile-bound reason; the self-approval detector's output contains no `as` override and no suggested approve call;
[ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-10.core reached from the MCP posture) + e2e;
[ ] consumers: every MCP host, fa-ohe, fa-z5u (fad-hosted MCP);
[ ] no-claim boundary: launch configuration is trusted operator input; this does not authenticate the operator (fa-v62/fa-r3q do).

TESTS: crates/fa-mcp/tests/e2e_stdio.rs cases above with the full JSON-RPC transcript logged on failure; registry.rs unit tests replacing the current `grant`/`yes` pass-through test (the old test is restated, not deleted: it becomes the negative); detect.rs unit test for the new self-approval text.

title: Teller reconciliation: bank statement parsers to BankLine documents with import receipts, matching engine as adaptive decisions with decision cards and a deterministic pinned fallback, journaled Match objects with exact residual explanations, reconciliation register verified by fold with RegisterEquals attestations, three-way matching, fa bank import / fa reconcile
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-10, CobaltGull): Teller is bank reconciliation: bank statement parsers producing BankLine documents (W4), a matching engine whose heuristics are adaptive decisions with decision cards and a deterministic pinned fallback (AGENTS.md adaptive-decision contract), a reconciliation register and attestations. At 96d1918 there is no Teller code (2 prose hits). fa-ff6 (bank feeds through flywheel_connectors) presumes BankLine documents and the matching engine, so it depends on this bead. Reconciliation is also one of Lantern's procedures and one of the registers the plan verifies by fold.

WHAT:
1. Bank statement parsers in `fa-formats` (interop) for CSV/OFX/CAMT.053 subsets, exact amounts (fa-money), every line a content-addressed `BankLine` document (Docket) with the statement's import receipt (Docket slice 2) and `DERIVED_FROM` the statement document; fuzzed readers.
2. `crates/fa-teller` (analytics): candidate generation (amount, date window, counterparty normalization, reference tokens), scoring as an adaptive decision: the decision card records the policy epoch, state space, candidates, observed features, the expected-benefit interval and the pinned fallback (exact amount + date within N days + reference equality, deterministic tie-break by lowest entry ordinal); learned scores are advisory features only; the card never changes a committed amount.
3. Match decisions as journaled, immutable objects (`Match { bank_line_ref, entry_ref | None, decision_card_ref, principal }`), one-to-many and many-to-one with exact residual explanations (fees, FX) that must be posted as their own entries under a named law, never absorbed; unmatching is a new object with lineage.
4. The reconciliation register: per bank account × period, book balance vs statement balance with the outstanding items list as a fold of matches and bank lines; `fa verify reconciliation` refolds it; reconciliation attestations bind `cell_key + fold_digest` (RegisterEquals).
5. Three-way matching (PO/receipt/invoice) as the same engine over documents, registered as a Lantern procedure.
6. CLI: `fa bank import <file> --account <code> --json`, `fa reconcile <account> --for <period> [--dry-run] --json` (plans the matches as intents with certificates; `--yes` or confirm_plan to commit), `fa reconcile status`.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: on a fixture statement every unambiguous line matches under the pinned fallback alone (learned features disabled) and the register folds to the statement balance; replaying the decision cards reproduces every match bit-for-bit; [ ] planted negatives: a card whose fallback is removed is refused at registration; a match that would change an amount is refused; a fee residual not posted under a law leaves the register out of balance and `verify reconciliation` says so; [ ] proof class: invariant (register-equals-fold, card replay) + statistical (match quality on the labelled corpus); [ ] consumers: fa-ff6, Lantern reconciliation procedure, CPAs; [ ] no-claim boundary: a reconciled register proves matches were recorded and the fold ties, not that every match is economically correct.

TESTS: parser tests with exact-amount vectors, fa-teller unit tests on labelled corpora with per-line logs, fa-reference naive matcher differential for the fallback, CLI binary tests.

description: WHY (TopazOsprey 3656, 2026-10-11, unverified observation during fa-txf t8): fa-cli's book_dir passes --book / FA_BOOK through raw. asupersync's UnixVfs::rename runs validate_safe_path (fs/path_ops.rs ~189), which refuses any '..' component, while create_dir_all and open do not validate; so a book opened as --book ../acme most likely fails at the substrate's first staging rename (fgdb-strata store.rs ~1014) or the blob store's rename, with an I/O error instead of a usable book. Agents are the primary operators and relative spellings are what they type. WHAT: (1) resolve the book directory once at the CLI boundary (fa-cli book_dir): join to the process cwd and normalize '.' and '..' lexically (no symlink resolution, no host canonicalize of a path that may not exist yet), refuse a path that escapes nothing but still carries '..' only if the normalized form cannot be produced; pass the normalized absolute path to Book::open and to the daemon request (through_daemon already prefers files.cwd); (2) the same normalization in fad's request handling so a daemon-side open sees the same path; (3) first verify the failure with a binary test (fa book create --book ../x from a temp cwd) and keep that test as the planted negative turned positive. ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: --book ../acme, --book ./acme and --book /abs/acme produce byte-identical robot envelopes (coordinate.book, data) for the same book; [ ] planted negative: before the fix the '..' spelling fails at the substrate rename (recorded in the test's doc as the observed defect), after the fix no substrate call ever sees a '..' component (a FaultVfs or path-recording VFS asserts it); [ ] proof class: invariant (one normalization point) + binary test; [ ] consumers: every agent invocation of fa with a relative --book, fad clients, the MCP posture (fa-mcp forwards cwd); [ ] no-claim boundary: this does not make the substrate tolerate '..'; it keeps such paths out of it.

title: Close engine: CloseRun/CloseTask DAG, incremental YearEndClose (Closing class) under the chart's closes_to map, FA-INV-03.nominal-zero, `fa close dry-run|run|status`, `fa verify close`, reclose deltas, rehearsal on a scratch book
description:
WHY: plan §7.5 "The close as a graph" — a CloseRun is a control object for (book, period) with CloseTask vertices and DEPENDS_ON edges (reconcile, accrue, depreciate, revalue, allocate, intercompany, eliminate, roll forward, produce statements, attest, lock); "every close is first rehearsed on a branch"; year-end Closing-class entries are real, incremental (each run closes the not-yet-closed net of every nominal account to closes_to — retained earnings, AOCI, fund balance), and FA-INV-03 `nominal-zero` requires Σ nominal balances for the year = 0 after the latest Closing entry (`fa verify close FY2026`). §15.6's first worked workflow ("The agent closes a month") and the README (`fa close dry-run --period 2026-03 --draft close-2026-03`) depend on it. At e606b46: the Closing class is refused FA-REF-102 (crates/fa-journal/src/post.rs:259); CloseRun exists only as a symbol id; `closes_to` is not on AccountRow; nominal-zero is dormant (registries/invariants.toml); no close verb exists. No bead covers the close engine (fa-xwv specifies stock/flow fold semantics; fa-9ae mentions closing identities only as test expectations).

WHAT: (1) chart: `closes_to` on Account (or a per-chart map) as a journaled schema effect; nominal account types per registries/account_types.toml. (2) Closing class admitted per Appendix C (W(close) in Open/SoftClosed, W(close,1) in Closed, W(restate,2) inside an Approved case in Locked) with the incremental law: closing legs = − (fold of nominal legs effective in FY − prior Closing legs) per account/unit/entity, to closes_to; zero-delta reclose emits nothing; income-statement folds carry exclude_classes [Closing] (fa-xwv). (3) CloseRun lifecycle object (Appendix A) with CloseTask vertices and a task registry (registries/close_tasks.toml: id, depends_on, the procedure/rule/intent it runs, evidence requirement, approver role) — tasks that need unbuilt subsystems (revalue, eliminate, statements) are registered with status unsupported(bead) and the run refuses to mark them done, never skips them silently. (4) `fa close dry-run --period P` replays trunk into a scratch book (Book::replay_into_scratch exists, crates/fa-journal/src/scratch.rs) and executes every supported automated task there, reporting the resulting tb diff vs trunk and per-task outcomes with a certificate (fa-cqk); `fa close run` executes on trunk task by task (each task obtains a fresh basis, plan §5.10) under the close capability; `fa close status`. (5) `fa verify close <FY>`: nominal-zero at the known-at of the latest Closing entry, exit 8 otherwise. (6) fa-reference: naive incremental close + nominal-zero oracle; differential including post-close adjustments and reclose.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: FY with revenue/expense legs → close → nominal accounts fold to zero, retained earnings equals net income; an audit adjustment after close → reclose emits only the delta; dry-run on scratch leaves trunk's journal head unchanged; [ ] planted negatives: Closing posted by a principal without close → refused; a task depending on an unfinished task → run refuses; a hand-made Closing entry that does not zero nominals → `fa verify close` exit 8; [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-03.nominal-zero live) + differential; [ ] consumers: §15.6 workflow, fa-9ae statements, fa-y4v, AS ORIGINALLY REPORTED (first Lock); [ ] no-claim boundary: mechanical close; materiality and treatment judgments stay outside (§0.2).

TESTS: fa-journal kernel tests, fa-reference differential with seeds, CLI binary tests for dry-run/run/status/verify close with robot transcripts.

title: fa-query: the FrankenAccounting GQL profile (FOR PERIOD, AS KNOWN AT, EFFECTIVE AT|BETWEEN, AT BRANCH, AS ORIGINALLY REPORTED, AS CURRENTLY STATED, AS REPORTED IN, CALL fa.*, EXPLAIN (CERTIFICATE)) rewritten onto substrate GQL, authorization before observation, read procedures bound to the register folds with certificates, the runtime graph (sessions, capabilities, drafts, findings, decision cards, access events) queryable read-only, fa query verb
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-10, CobaltGull): The plan's query language is GQL through the substrate plus the namespaced FrankenAccounting profile (`FOR PERIOD`, `AS KNOWN AT`, `EFFECTIVE AT|BETWEEN`, `AT BRANCH`, `AS ORIGINALLY REPORTED`, `AS CURRENTLY STATED`, `AS REPORTED IN <certificate>`, `CALL fa.*`, `EXPLAIN (CERTIFICATE)`), and AGENTS.md requires the system's own runtime (sessions, capabilities, drafts, close runs, findings, decision cards, access events) to be a read-only, access-controlled graph queryable in GQL. At 96d1918 no GQL is executed anywhere (fgdb_gql is used once, for the symbol resolver); `fa query` does not exist. The library's `query` certified read is part of the product shape.

WHAT:
1. `crates/fa-query` (surface layer): the profile parser as a thin front that rewrites the FrankenAccounting clauses into substrate GQL with explicit known-at and effective predicates over the entry/period graph (the clauses are sugar over properties the graph already has: recorded CommitSeq, effective_date, period refs, branch id), refusing anything the profile does not name (exit 3) with the admissible form in the refusal.
2. `CALL fa.*` procedures: `fa.trial_balance`, `fa.balance`, `fa.explain_balance`, `fa.open_items`, `fa.fold` as registered read procedures bound to the same folds fa-registers uses; results carry the coordinate and a certificate when `EXPLAIN (CERTIFICATE)` is requested (the certificate commits to the query text, coordinate and result digest; `fa replay` re-executes).
3. Authorization precedes observation: the capability's caveats (books, accounts subtree, periods, known_at ≤ seq, branch, partial_view) are applied by refusing before query construction in the interim posture (doctrine 8), never as a result filter; whole-entry visibility rules from fa-llx apply.
4. The runtime graph: sessions, capabilities (with revocation), drafts, close runs, findings, decision cards and access events are already or become graph objects; `fa query` can read them under a capability with the `read` op and the matching scope; every read is an access event (journaled, append-only).
5. CLI/library: `Book::query(&cap, text) -> QueryResult`, `fa query "<gql>" --json`, robot events `rows`, `certificate`; byte-deterministic ordering.
6. `AS ORIGINALLY REPORTED` / `AS CURRENTLY STATED` and `AS REPORTED IN <certificate>` bind to the palimpsest registers and statement certificates when those land; until then they refuse naming their bead (never a silent fallback).

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: `fa query "MATCH ... FOR PERIOD 2026-03 AS KNOWN AT 120 CALL fa.trial_balance"` returns rows equal to `fa tb --for 2026-03 --known-at 120` byte-for-byte and `EXPLAIN (CERTIFICATE)` yields a replayable certificate; a query over the runtime graph lists the caller's own session; [ ] planted negatives: a capability scoped to one account subtree refuses a query naming another before any read (no storage observation, proven by a lab VFS read counter); a clause outside the profile is refused with the admissible form; a result-filter implementation (mutation) fails the no-observation test; [ ] proof class: invariant (authorization-before-observation, FA-INV-10) + differential (query vs register folds); [ ] consumers: agents (A6), auditors pinned to a known-at, fa-mcp resources, the dogfooded runtime graph; [ ] no-claim boundary: the profile proves parity with the folds for the covered procedures, not general GQL completeness.

TESTS: parser goldens, kernel-level authorization tests with the read counter, differential vs fa-registers and fa-reference, CLI binary tests with query text and coordinate logged.

title: Evidence intake pipeline: derived text Documents from owner tools run as subprocess graders (franken_ocr focr, franken_whisper fw robot), deterministic PDF text-layer extraction, DERIVED_FROM lineage, honest grading
description:
WHY: Bet A3 is only as strong as what can become a Document. Scanned invoices, bank PDFs and recorded calls become evidence only as Documents with lineage and an honest grade. franken_ocr (focr CLI: robot JSON with layout boxes; 19.3% CER on its own corpus — advisory only) and franken_whisper (fw robot run: NDJSON transcripts with diarization) link fsqlite and other closures FA cannot carry, so they run as SEPARATE PROCESSES exactly as the plan runs hledger/bean-check. hedge_fund_data_tool has deterministic PDF text-layer extraction (crates/hfdt-sources/src/extract.rs pdf_text_to_text; explicitly no OCR) and hfdt-pdf-crypto (AES-256 PDFs with empty password; deps aes+sha2 only) that should be extracted upstream into standalone owner crates; frankengit's fgit-deflate (std-only bounded streaming zlib) decodes FlateDecode streams for the in-house PDF reader.
WHAT: depends on fa-lp6 (Document objects). `fa document add <file> --extract text|ocr|transcript`: the original bytes are the content-addressed Document; each extraction is a derived Document with a grade (TextLayer = deterministic; OCR/transcript = advisory, AgentUpload-equivalent) and a DERIVED_FROM edge carrying tool name, version, model artifact hash and command line. Extraction runs under a Cx with filesystem/process capability only in the facade/CLI posture, never in the kernel; results are journaled as documents, never as amounts. TextLayer re-derives bit-for-bit under replay; OCR/ASR are marked non-replayable. Pin fgit-deflate by git rev now; hfdt crates only after upstream extraction.
ACCEPTANCE: [ ] text-layer golden on a fixture PDF; [ ] encrypted-PDF fixture; [ ] OCR/ASR adapters invoke the external binary only when present (UNRUN otherwise, never a fake); [ ] no amount is parsed from derived text into a leg; [ ] `fa explain evidence <entry>` walks DERIVED_FROM. UPSTREAM: hedge_fund_data_tool — extract PDF text-layer + pdf-crypto into standalone crates without chrono/serde; franken_ocr/franken_whisper — stable robot JSON schema with version + artifact hash in output.
notes:
Upstream issue filed 2026-10-10: https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/hedge_fund_data_tool/issues/1 (standalone PDF text-layer + pdf-crypto crates).
TESTING (idea-wizard pass 1): every slice lands unit tests in the owning crate AND an end-to-end script-level test (binary test in crates/fa-cli/tests/cli.rs where a verb is involved) with detailed, greppable logging of inputs, digests, and verdicts; external tools absent => UNRUN, never a fake pass; gate stays rch-only.

title: Reports read registers: watermark + exact tail fold for tb/explain/open-items (no full-book scan per report), fad-supervised maintainer woken after each commit, and a complexity witness proving report cost is independent of unrelated history
description:
WHY: plan §5.3 "A balance read at the head is register(cell) ⊕ fold(legs of cell in (watermark, head]) … reads are O(1) at the watermark plus a bounded tail scan"; the maintainer "run[s] as a supervised region woken by fad after each commit"; §17 gates (balance read p99 < 50 µs; TB of 100k accounts < 200 ms). At e606b46 every report and explain is a full `vertices_at` scan of the whole book (crates/fa-registers/src/lib.rs:910 report_at, :228-252 entries_at) and the maintainer (fa-vn4) is reachable only from the library with nothing calling it automatically; registers are a write-only cache only the verifier reads (registers audit). This is correct but O(book) per read — every report gets slower forever.

WHAT: reports consume maintained cells at the watermark plus an exact tail fold over delta_since (bounded by max_tail_legs; beyond it, refold or advance first — never serve a partial answer); every report states served_at_watermark, tail_length (§17's own law); certificates (fa-cqk) record the watermark and tail; fad wakes the maintainer after each commit as a supervised asupersync region (no detached thread); a complexity witness test: a TB over a fixed small cell set must perform O(cells + tail) substrate reads regardless of 10k unrelated entries (substrate read counter).

title: Define control-record encoding and immutable lifecycle projections
description:
References: §§4.2, 5.10, 7.3, 8.3, 10.2, Appendix A/C/F (lines 286-317, 435, 483, 540, 606-620, 1144, 1200-1207, 1278-1279, 1329).
Every Entry requires 2 or more posting legs, including SchemaControl/PolicyControl/PeriodControl in the same EntryClass union. Creating the first chart/calendar/book or opening a Future period has no legitimate pair of posting legs. Encoding invented zero-value accounting legs would violate the no-prototype/no-fabricated-leg doctrine. Define a journal record union or a precisely class-dependent payload with control effects separate from posting legs.
Lifecycle objects are declared immutable after commit (FA-INV-02), yet Period.state is a versioned property, RestatementCase/CloseRun/Finding/DraftSet carry changing status, Capability carries revoked, and §5.10 compare-and-sets membership counters. Specify which immutable transition records are authoritative and which current-state objects are disposable projections, with reconstruction and known-at rules. Attestations on a Register must bind its coordinate/value digest rather than merely a mutable/rebuildable cell identity.
Negative examples: create an empty book and first account without fake legs; transition case Proposed→Approved→Posted without updating its original payload; rebuild lifecycle state from immutable transitions. W1-W4, G0.
Model follow-up: entity-scoped capabilities and cash-by-legal-entity registers require an authoritative entity assignment. Entry/Account/Leg schemas and declared edges do not identify an owning LegalEntity, and the Dimension kind list has no mandatory legal-entity dimension. Either constrain each book to one declared entity or specify the balanced entity dimension and membership checks; do not infer ownership from descriptions.
notes:
Addressed in ff3b6eb: §4.1 immutability model (payload objects / lifecycle-by-transition objects with projected status / rebuildable projections); control classes carry legs=[] and a typed ControlPayload union (Appendix A); FA-INV-02 clauses payload-immutable, lifecycle-by-transition, control-record; LegalEntity.code and Book.entities with legal_entity as a mandatory balancing dimension (per-entity clause of FA-INV-01, §5.2); RegisterEquals binds cell_key + fold_digest (§9.4). title: fa-canon first slice: typed total rule language, type checker and IR, journaled content-addressed rule versions with dual-control activation, interim evaluator under a stripped Cx (no clock/entropy/net/fs, compile-fail proven), rule families bound to intents (Accrue/Defer, Allocation, Revaluation, Elimination) replacing their FA-REF-102 class refusals, golden corpora, backtesting on drafts, VM adapter boundary
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-10, CobaltGull): Canon (W6) is the posting-rule engine: a rule language, type checker and IR, an interim evaluator under a stripped `Cx` (no clock, entropy, network or filesystem), the intent catalog bound to rule families, golden corpora, backtesting and activation with dual control. At 96d1918 there is no Canon code at all (fa-model/src/canon.rs is the byte codec; "Canon" appears twice as forward references); Allocation/Revaluation/Elimination entry classes are refused as not implemented because no rule can produce them. Doctrine 3's sharpest instance ("a rule that wants today receives it as a declared input") has nothing to bind to. Canon depends on the intents slice (rule-driven intents are typed intents) and on W3's period law.

WHAT (first real slice):
1. `crates/fa-canon` (laws layer; pure): the rule language as a small, total, typed expression language over declared inputs (event fields, registered units, account codes, dates given as inputs), with a parser, a type checker that refuses floats and unregistered units/laws, and an IR; every rounding or allocation in a rule names a registered law from `rounding_laws.toml`.
2. Rule versions as journaled, content-addressed objects (Appendix A `RuleVersion`): source, IR digest, declared inputs, produced entry classes, activation state; activation is a PolicyControl-style control record under dual control (two distinct principals, SoD row), with `GENERATED_BY` lineage from every entry a rule produces to the rule version and `DERIVED_FROM` to the event.
3. The interim evaluator: `evaluate(rule_version, event, inputs) -> Vec<Intent>` under a stripped Cx (type-level: the evaluator's context carries no capability for clock/entropy/net/fs, proven by a compile-fail test); re-running version v over event e reproduces the entry digest (the plan's testable-derivation claim) as a test.
4. Rule families bound to intents: Accrue/Defer, Allocation (largest-remainder over a named law), Revaluation (FX law from fa-p7r), Elimination (Concordat); each family's produced class is enabled in the kernel's class gate only when its rule family exists (replacing the FA-REF-102 refusal for that class with the real path).
5. Golden corpora: checked-in events + expected intents per rule family; backtesting = replaying a rule version over a historical event range on a draft (fa-s7x) and diffing against the live entries; dry-run plans for every produced intent (fa-intents).
6. VM adapter boundary: the evaluator is behind a trait so the substrate's UDF VM (Appendix H, R-VM) can replace it with the registered switch-over rule; no substrate code copied.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: an Accrue rule produces an Adjusting intent whose entry replays byte-identically from (rule version, event); an Allocation rule's residual lands on the named rounding account under the named law; activation without a second principal is refused by SoD; [ ] planted negatives: a rule source that reads a clock-like input not declared fails type checking; a rule naming an unregistered law is refused; a mutated IR digest fails the lineage check; [ ] proof class: invariant (derivation replay) + golden corpora; [ ] consumers: Allocation/Revaluation/Elimination classes, fa-statements consolidation, agents' intent catalog; [ ] no-claim boundary: Canon proves rules are deterministic and typed, not that any rule encodes the right accounting policy.

TESTS: fa-canon unit tests for parser/type checker/IR with goldens, kernel tests for lineage and activation SoD, differential vs a fa-reference naive evaluator for the first families, logs naming the rule version digest.

title: Reconcile CLI, schema, determinism, and public comparison contradictions
description:
References: §§0/3.2, 4.7, 9.4, 13.2, 15.3-15.7, 18.2/18.4, Appendix A/C/D; README examples/comparison.
- §4.7 and FA-REF-015 refuse instants as effective dates, while §15.3 silently converts with a warning. Pick one explicit policy. Period inadmissibility is exit 2 in Genesis but listed under exit 7 too.
- CLI fa hold is both financial hold and governance hold place/release; MCP catalog has no complete governance/registry/interop/lifecycle mapping despite parity claim. Declare unambiguous verbs and shared-operation mappings or registered exclusions.
- Closed/Locked matrix permits Resolution(Voids), Revision and Reopen, but §7.3/FA-INV-03 says only restatement classes; matrix requires post_softclosed, migrate, schema_change absent from the §14.2 closed op vocabulary. Reconcile from one registry.
- Bundles claim same scope+checkpoint yields same bytes but include producer, produced_at_seq, capability and redaction fields; bind the complete closure or split deterministic content from production receipt. Fixed-as_known_at RegisterEquals assertions cannot become false from later entries; use a separate head-following reconciliation monitor and retain the original assertion.
- §15.5 example needs IS edges, Subledger→Account CONTROLS, LegalEntity.code and Leg.effective_date not declared in the model. Fix the model/query contract and reject cross-unit sums in the accounting GQL profile.
- fa-formats/qbo and object_schemas/tracing/conversion laws need explicit registry ownership; ftui and fsci_stats are promised despite the closed four-foundation policy. Reconcile their inclusion/exclusion with explicit posture/test-only policy, never silent allowlist expansion.
- Plan/README characterize all ERP posted journals as editable rows. Oracle Fusion documentation explicitly says a posted journal cannot be changed and describes reversal workflows: https://docs.oracle.com/cloud/131/user_services/FAFTT/F416502AN10266.htm . Narrow competitive claims and separate existing derived balance caches from authoritative mutable accounting facts. SEC audit-trail amendments were adopted October 12, 2022, not 2023 as §0 says: https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2022-187 .
Acceptance: schema-backed examples, deterministic bundle repeat across callers/times under declared closure, immutable assertion vs head-monitor example, one exit per refusal, complete verb mappings, source-backed comparison language. W4/W5/W9, G0/G3.
notes: Addressed in ff3b6eb: instants refused (FA-REF-015) never converted; exits reconciled (period inadmissibility = 7, accounting-law = 3; Genesis text fixed; dictionary a strict superset of fgdb's); Reserve/PostReserve/VoidReserve so fa hold is governance only; MCP clusters fa.book/chart/govern/io with a total verbs.toml mapping and two registered exclusions; §7.3/FA-INV-03 Locked wording; §14.2 closed ops list; ProductionReceipt split from the deterministic bundle body; immutable RegisterEquals + drift monitor; §15.5 example uses REPRESENTS/CONTROLS/LegalEntity.code/effective_day and per-unit sums; §18.2 registry ownership rows; ftui excluded from 1.0 and fsci_stats on a test-only allowlist; §0/§3.2 ERP claims narrowed; SEC date fixed. Left open for re-review.

title: Certified trial balance and `fa replay <certificate>` (FA-INV-11.core): Certificate over Database::execute_certified inputs, byte-identical replay, `fa certificate status` — the Genesis acceptance item no bead in fa-lm7's graph owns
description:
WHY: plan §19 Genesis slice ends "… `fa tb --json` returns the certified trial balance → … → `fa replay` reproduces the trial balance bytes"; G1 requires FA-INV-11.core live. At e606b46 the robot envelope's `certificate` is always null (crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:231), there is no `fa replay` verb, `Database::execute_certified` and `Database::replay` are never called (the substrate is used only through point reads, scans and delta_since), and both FA-INV-11 clauses are dormant (registries/invariants.toml). The only bead that mentions replay is fa-9ae (the full statements engine, P1, unassigned, depends on fa-xwv) — and fa-lm7 does not depend on it, so Genesis can never close as specified. This bead is the Genesis-sized slice: certify the reports that exist (tb, explain balance, open-items) before the statements engine.

WHAT: (1) `Certificate` object per §13.6/Appendix A: closure {book root = substrate snapshot_identity (chain commitment at seq), branch, known_at seq, effective selector, report definition id+version (tb/explain/open-items as built-in definitions), parameters digest, registry epochs (units, laws, admissibility, symbols), capability commitment (fa-0x0) or "embedded-owner"}, `inputs: [NativeResultCertificate]` for every substrate read in the closure, output_digest (BLAKE3 of the canonical output bytes), replay_command, completeness_grade. (2) Reads inside a certified report go through `Database::execute_certified` (a native read returning NativeResultCertificate) — or, if the report's fold cannot be expressed as native certified reads yet, the certificate records the literal-fold inputs it used (entry vids + digests in the selected prefix, i.e. the accumulator range) and labels `replay_scope = "fa-fold-over-prefix"`; either way replay is exact and the scope is stated. (3) Certificates persisted lazily on request (`--certify` or always for --json; decide and register) as content-addressed objects (operation_costs row). (4) `fa replay <certificate-oid|file> --json`: re-executes (Database::replay per native input, then the fold) and compares output_digest; mismatch exit 8 naming the first differing row. (5) `fa certificate status <oid>`: Current | SupersededBy (entries recorded after the known-at with effective dates inside the selector). (6) Robot envelope `certificate` non-null for certified reads; robot-schema pin bump. (7) FA-INV-11.core live with checker + planted negative.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: `fa tb --period P --json` → certificate c; `fa replay c` exit 0 byte-identical on the same machine and on a second worker (cross-machine digest compared in the gate); after a backdated post into P, `fa certificate status c` = SupersededBy and `fa replay c` still reproduces the original bytes at its known-at; [ ] planted negatives: tamper the certificate's parameters → replay exit 8; tamper a journal entry in the prefix (test adversary) → replay exit 8; replay at a different known-at refused; [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-11.core) + replay CI; [ ] consumers: fa-9ae (statements build on this), fa-l3c bundles, fa-y4v damages, examiners (§15.6 "fa replay reproduces each figure later"); [ ] no-claim boundary: replay proves the same closure yields the same bytes; it does not prove the closure's entries are economically right.

TESTS: fa-cli binary tests for tb/explain/open-items certification and replay with certificates logged; fa-registers unit tests for canonical output encoding; a cross-worker determinism step in check.sh (two runs, digests compared).

title: Specify N-leg hold resolution, reserved availability, and expiry-period behavior
description:
References: §§5.4/5.5, 7.6, Appendix A/B/C/F/G (lines 409-415, 495, 1175, 1242, 1268, 1342, 1374).
Posts { amount: Amount } generalizes a two-leg TigerBeetle transfer inadequately to N-leg/multi-unit holds. A pending USD entry D A60, D B40, C cash100 resolved for 60 admits D A60/C cash60 or D A20/D B40/C cash60, both balanced and under original legs. Neither schema nor law chooses. Multiple currencies cannot fit one Amount. Require a per-leg balanced subvector, named proportional law, or explicit registered absence.
Limit reads say head net balance but do not define worst-case reserved availability. With cash100, a pending outflow80 must block a second80 and an unrelated posted outflow30; pending inflow cannot finance an outflow before resolution. Specify reserve/consume/release equations and atomic witnesses.
Pending created in Open can encounter Closed/Locked before timeout. Appendix C allows only Voids in Locked, excluding Expires; §5.4 requires Expires for every elapsed deadline, so the sweep can become permanently inadmissible. title: Kernel refuses unverified envelope/payload fields: `base_totals: Some`, caller-supplied `plan_certificate`, and non-Intent origins (Rule/Sweep/Schedule/Control) on the public post path
description:
WHY (verified at e606b46): (a) `base_totals` is never read by the posting kernel — there is no reference to it in crates/fa-journal/src/post.rs; `EntryProposal::validate` checks only its shape (crates/fa-model/src/entry.rs:1499-1516). Because legs' `base_amount` is refused (post.rs:441-445 "refused, never admitted unchecked"), a proposal can still carry `base_totals: Some { unit_id, debits, credits, fx_law_oid, rate_doc_oids, residual }` with arbitrary functional-currency totals and fictitious law/rate ids, and they are journaled forever. (b) `plan_certificate` is an unchecked caller-supplied id (post.rs:92, sealed into the envelope at :1612) bound into entry_digest; Appendix A requires it to be None for rule-, sweep-, control- and migration-origin entries and to name a verified PlanCertificate otherwise — no certificate exists yet (fa-we7). (c) `EntryOrigin` is validated only for Migration (post.rs:381-402): a library caller can post an Intent-class entry claiming `Rule { rule_version_oid, event_ref, inputs_digest }`, `Sweep`, or `Schedule` origin — forged provenance; schedule verification keys on that origin (crates/fa-journal/src/schedule.rs:1280). The CLI always builds Intent (crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:2574), so the hole is in the embedded API and every future surface.

WHAT: in the posting pipeline's step 1 (before any read): refuse `base_totals.is_some()` with not_implemented("entry.base_totals") citing fa-p7r/fa-s3c until the FX law reads it; refuse `plan_certificate.is_some()` until fa-we7's verifier exists (then: verify it, and require None for non-Intent origins); refuse any origin other than Intent on the public `post` path, with Rule (until Canon, fa-c34), Sweep and Schedule minted only by their internal constructors (sweep.rs / schedule.rs) through a crate-private entry point that the public API cannot reach. title: fad tick/sweep scheduler and CLI timing intents: the clock and the System authority live in fad only (plan §5.4; no fa tick/sweep, no --grant system in the embedded CLI)
description:
WHY (CobaltGull ruling 2026-10-11 01:3xZ on JadePeak 3346): plan §5.4 says "the fa daemon orders one ExpirySweep control entry per configured tick carrying rollback-resistant time evidence". The kernel side is landed (fa-ctf: record_tick with TickRequest, sweep/sweep_batch under the book's System principal, due_holds/due_reversals, scheduled reversals by identity) but nothing drives it: fa post still refuses timeout_ns, with_auto_reverse has no CLI, and no posture records ticks. Doctrine 3 and 6 fix where the clock may live: a posting rule never reads the wall clock, recorded time is never user-supplied, and the lab runtime's virtual clock is the only legitimate control of the ticks. The embedded `fa` CLI therefore never reads a clock and never mints System authority; fad, as the posture that owns the writer lease, does both.

WHAT:
1. fad scheduler: a `[daemon] tick_ns` row in registries/verbs.toml; fad reads its own clock under its Cx (clock capability granted to fad only), records one TimeEvidence tick per interval through `Book::record_tick(observed_utc_ns, capability)` with the System capability it derives from the book's keys as lease holder, then runs one bounded sweep (`Book::sweep(capability, max_batch)`) and one bounded scheduled-reversal batch; `fad sweep-now` for an operator-requested cycle; every cycle is journaled as the existing control records, nothing else.
2. Book adapters (fa crate): record_tick / sweep / sweep_reversals taking the capability; the principal is the capability's holder, which the kernel requires to be System; describe = seal_text, fallible (KernelError::Entropy propagates, txn.abort() first, per 3303/3304); no principal argument from the caller; never mint System in an adapter.
3. fa CLI: post intents gain `timeout_ns` (Pending) and `reverse_on` (Adjusting) as data only; `fa triage` reports due_holds / due_reversals / blocked_reversals and names the next step ("start fad serve --book <dir>; it ticks and sweeps"); there is NO `fa tick`, NO `fa sweep`, and NO `--grant system` in the embedded CLI (an ambient-authority escape hatch, refused by design).
4. Refusals: a sweep request without the System capability is the existing 013; a tick with a non-monotonic observation follows the registered tick law (094–098); a daemon without a clock capability refuses to start its scheduler with a typed error naming the posture.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: under the lab runtime's virtual time a Pending with timeout_ns expires on the first tick past its deadline via fad's scheduler and `fa triage` then reports zero due; an Adjusting with reverse_on is reversed by the scheduled batch at the period open; a `fad sweep-now` sweeps exactly the due population under max_batch_entries; [ ] planted negatives: the embedded CLI has no verb that records a tick (parity test over verbs.toml); an adapter that accepts a caller-supplied principal fails the kernel's System check (013); an entropy failure in describe aborts the transaction and leaves frontier, cursor, resolution and reversal unchanged, then a retry succeeds; a wall-clock read anywhere outside fad's scheduler fails the Cx capability audit; [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-15.expiry live, recorded-time-never-user-supplied) + lab-runtime simulation; [ ] consumers: operators running fad, agents reading triage, G2; [ ] no-claim boundary: virtual-time proofs show the scheduler's law, not wall-clock accuracy of a production host.

TESTS: fad lab tests under virtual time (tick → expiry → triage zero; scheduled reversal at open; sweep-now bounded), fa-cli binary tests for the new intent fields and triage lines with transcripts logged, parity test that verbs.toml has no tick/sweep verb for the embedded posture, Cx capability audit test.

title: control_kinds registry: register EntryOrigin::Control.control_kind (1 chart install … 8 capability revocation) in entry_classes.toml with a fa-registry reader, module constants replaced by registry symbols, totality/uniqueness gate, kernel class/kind cross-check
description:
WHY (TopazOsprey 3348/3353, CobaltGull ruling 2026-10-11 01:4xZ): `EntryOrigin::Control.control_kind` is a durable field in every control record's origin, but it is not registered anywhere; each module defines its own constant. At 26fa0cb the value 4 already carries two meanings (the TimeControl tick in sweep.rs and the PolicyControl capability revocation in policy.rs), and the unlanded fa-txf A had claimed 4 a third time. Nothing dispatches on the value today, because the class does, but a durable origin whose numbers are ambiguous cannot be read by fa-verify, Lantern or a migration without guessing. Doctrine 9 forbids serde-derived enums as durable formats; the registered-symbol pattern (symbols.toml, entry classes, refusal codes) is the house answer.

WHAT:
1. A `[[control_kinds]]` table in registries/entry_classes.toml with the eight rows: 1 chart_install, 2 period_transition, 3 policy_activation, 4 time_tick, 5 schedule_cancel, 6 import_run, 7 legal_hold, 8 capability_revocation; each row names its control class and the module that mints it.

3. Every module constant (sweep.rs, schedule.rs, policy.rs, the chart and period transition sites, fa-txf's import and hold) replaced by the registry symbol; a workspace grep test (or the registries gate step) refuses a literal `control_kind: <int>` outside the registry reader.
4. MistyPlateau moves capability revocation from 4 to 8 (no users; the durable value changes in place, no shim); fa-txf A uses 6, C1 uses 7.
5. fa-reference mirrors the table literally (its own copy of the eight pairs) so the differential catches a drift between the engine's origin bytes and the registry.

title: substrate: fgdb-sim FaultFile::sync_dirents retires namespace debts BEFORE the fallible backing open/sync_all returns (vfs.rs ~1313) — a failed or cancelled barrier can leave an unfenced name retained across a simulated crash; upstream fix with per-op identities captured before the first await and same-generation retirement after the real barrier
description: WHY (WhiteCreek 3706 / GoldenHollow 3621, 2026-10-11, source review of fgdb-sim at the pinned rev and the private alias candidate a3a636bd): FaultFile::sync_dirents removes the directory's namespace debts and only then awaits the backing open + sync_all. If the backing call fails or the future is cancelled, the debts are already gone, so a later simulated crash wrongly retains the unfenced name; the simulator then certifies durability the real filesystem would not give. Moving the removal after the await alone is also wrong: a concurrent operation that adds a new debt between the capture and the retirement would be cleared by the older barrier. This is separate from the alias/absolute-path repair in fa-n4m and must not be conflated with it. Doctrine 10: fixed upstream in frankengraphdb, never patched here. WHAT (design from 3706): (1) capture stable per-op debt identities (e.g. an Arc token compared by ptr_eq, or a generation number) under the lock BEFORE the first await, preserving the empty-debt and lie-trigger behaviours; (2) await the real backing barrier; (3) under the lock again, retire only the captured same-generation debts; an Err or a cancellation leaves every debt in place; an older generation's barrier cannot retire a newer debt. (4) Upstream PR with probes, then the joint fgdb/fgdb-sim re-pin here (franken-stack.lock), then re-run every FaultVfs regression. ACCEPTANCE (probes, all upstream): [ ] backing reopen/sync failure preserves the debt and a crash loses the name; [ ] retry success survives the crash; [ ] pause after the real backing sync, add debt B, resume: A survives, B is lost; [ ] a second barrier that retires A before B defeats index reuse (identity, not position); [ ] a dropped paused future retains its debt; [ ] proof class: bounded_model (simulation) — no broader crash certification; [ ] consumers: fa-txf FaultVfs regression, fa-0fl crash campaign, fa-n4m re-pin; [ ] no-claim boundary: this makes the simulator honest about failed barriers; it says nothing new about the host filesystem. Deletion condition: closes when the upstream fix is re-pinned and the probes are live.

title: `fold_digest` per plan §5.3: BLAKE3 over canonical leg contributions in (commit_seq, entry_vid, ordinal) order, matching the accumulator's leaf order (today it hashes the summed cell)
description:
WHY: plan §5.3: "fold_digest is the BLAKE3 of the canonical leg contributions sorted by (commit_seq, entry_vid, ordinal), so it is also a commitment to commit order (it matches the accumulator's leaf order, §13.2), two registers that claim the same value from different histories cannot collide, and a recomputation can be compared by digest". At e606b46 the digest hashes the aggregated sums plus the watermark (crates/fa-registers/src/lib.rs:165-185; entity.rs:123-148), and the registered FA-INV-04 checker is `fold_digest_is_a_function_of_cells_and_watermark` (lib.rs:1046) — a test of the deviation, not of the plan. Two different histories with equal sums share a digest, and the fa-verify balance proof is not tied to it.

WHAT: streaming contribution digest (domain `fa:register-fold:v2`) maintained incrementally by the maintainer and recomputed by verify; register format version bump with the old format reported as needing rebuild (drift, never assumed equal); fa-verify's balance proof binds the same digest so an outsider can compare the producer's register digest to the recomputed one; replace the INV-04 checker with a test that two histories with equal sums produce different digests.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: maintained digest == rebuilt digest == fa-verify recomputed digest on fixtures; [ ] planted negatives: two equal-sum histories differ; reordered contributions differ; [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-04.core) ; [ ] consumers: fa-cqk certificates, fa-l3c bundles; [ ] no-claim boundary: digest binds contributions, not their economic correctness.

title: Close evidence-required and retention/erasure contract gaps
description:
References: §§8.5, 9.1/9.2/9.6, 10.2, 14.6, Appendix A/B/F (lines 548, 560-564, 580, 618, 795, 1152-1153, 1188-1194, 1232, 1254, 1332).
Common intent evidence is optional and Entry.evidence has no minimum or class-specific source contract. A registered Intent origin with an empty evidence list satisfies the written unknown-reference check vacuously, contrary to AGENTS' rule that an entry without registered evidence is unencodable. Define required real evidence by class (manual assertion/control authority may be explicit objects), and distinguish drafts from committable entries.
External documents retain locator+observed digest, not necessarily bytes. FA-INV-05 promises strong retention of the provenance closure for the retention floor. Specify durable custody requirements or a downgraded, non-equivalent external-evidence profile with failure behavior; a URL alone cannot ensure retention.
AttachEvidence appends edges after commit but Entry.evidence is digest-covered and immutable. Separate original posting evidence from later supplemental evidence, version the latter and specify how each closure is selected/certified.
Erasure promises no PII outside Party/Document, but immutable descriptions, leg memos, tags, external IDs, source-entered-by fields and structured event data can carry PII. Specify schema-level sensitive-field placement and key granularity; erasing a Party alone cannot remove those copies. Add live foundation ledger rows for erasure/retention/legal-hold capabilities rather than assuming them.
Acceptance: absent required evidence, lost external source, supplemental document after posting, PII in each allowed free-text location, legal hold vs erasure race, preservation of public amount commitments. W2/W4/Steward, G0.
Resolve provenance edge retention types too: bare substrate Oid/MarkerRef are identities, not retention edges. Appendix A imports a typed-reference law but uses bare Oids widely; enumerate strong/weak/cut-conditioned references and their erasure interaction so FA-INV-05 is actually enforceable.
notes:
Addressed in ff3b6eb: §9.2 evidence_policy.toml minimums per class (ManualAssertion with reason code as the honest alternative; NeedsEvidence drafts cannot promote), external evidence retains bytes by default with an attested ByReferenceOnly downgrade, SupplementalEvidence as a new object; §8.5 Erasable<T> fields (description, memo, tags, external ids, migration names, event attributes) under per-Party subject keys, hold/erasure race as a witness conflict; Appendix A reference law (strong/weak/locator) and Erasable schema; Appendix H R-ERASE/R-RED/R-KEY; FA-INV-05 clauses. Left open for re-review.

title: Preserve publication and historical identity in migration and scenario interim postures
description:
References: §§5.8, 8.6, 15.2, Appendix G/H (lines 427, 552, 833-835, 1371, 1376, 1395, 1402).
§5.8 promises staging followed by one atomic migration finalization. R-BULK's interim is ordinary committed WriteBatch chunks with manifests/resume; no staging visibility or finalization filter is defined. Readers may see an incomplete migration, and a later bad chunk cannot roll back already committed entries. Specify durable staging within the same engine, activation semantics and failure/retry visibility, without deleting history.
Scenario fallback replays trunk into a fresh open_memory database, whose assigned CommitSeq/HLC and allocated VIds differ. Entry digests embed book/branch/account identities, and approvals/certificates bind those digests. Pin original-coordinate provenance and identity translation or a read-only base-plus-overlay abstraction so replay does not forge recorded time or claim original membership. Replaying only accounting objects cannot reproduce physical sequences containing access logs/checkpoints/maintenance.
Close rehearsal needs computable draft balances before substrate branches exist, but §15.2 describes draft materialization as future optional and scratch replay only for scenarios. State the shared law for all draft report reads and for promotion changing head.
Restatement case posting is atomic in §8.3/§5.1 yet Appendix G allows a separate case-transition transaction. Place the entries and posted-state effect in one transaction or specify exact recoverable state and idempotency preventing repost.
Acceptance: invalid final migration chunk, crash around activation; scratch replay with intervening system records; draft-to-trunk digest/approval changes; crash after case entries before transition. W2-W4/W5, G0/G2.
notes: Addressed in ff3b6eb: §8.6 MigrationRun staging invisible until Finalize (Abandoned runs stay journaled and invisible; retries are new runs); §15.2 one scratch-book law for drafts and scenarios (accounting objects only, identity-derived vids and seq-free payloads preserve digests and approvals, SeqMap in the certificate, no forged membership); Appendix G restatement case post is one write_ordered transaction with its LifecycleTransition. Left open for re-review.

title: redaction caveat: Capability v2 tag 2 `redaction = <contract>`, conjunctive with `privileged` (confines a capability to a contract's redacted views)

title: Kernel refusal hygiene: balancing-leg approval binding, revocation witness before any observation, Locked fix hint, non-account vid as typed refusal, idempotent period-transition retry
description:
WHY (Folio audit of e606b46; each item cited): (D6) for Balancing posts, approvals bind the request-form digest (crates/fa-journal/src/limit.rs:681-692; post.rs:934-947) while the sealed entry's proposal_digest covers the resolved legs (post.rs:1606-1612) — plan §4.6 says approvals bind proposal_digest; decide and document which digest an approval of a balancing request binds (recommended: the resolved proposal, with the plan certificate from fa-we7 carrying the request form) and test it. (D7) a revoked capability can trigger book-spec/time-zone reads and their refusals (FA-REF-104/102 at post.rs:450-458, :544-547) before the revocation witness (post.rs:672), contrary to the comment at post.rs:670 and doctrine 8 — move the revocation/expiry witness first. (D8) the Locked-period refusal suggests Reversal/Adjusting with post_closed (post.rs:902-906), which Locked refuses — the fix must name the case-bound path or the next open period. (D9) a vid that is not an Account is decoded by `AccountRow::decode` and surfaces as KernelError::Corrupt (exit 5) instead of a typed refusal (post.rs:968-978) — add a label point read and refuse FA-REF-014 (unknown account) with exit 2. (D13) retrying an identical period transition is refused (crates/fa-journal/src/period.rs:138-146) instead of returning the recorded outcome (FA-INV-09 retry semantics).

WHAT: the five fixes above, each with its own planted negative; refusal catalog rows/fix texts updated; robot-schema pin only if an event shape changes.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] each item has one test that fails on e606b46 and passes after (old-code negative recorded in the commit message, as fa-40l did); [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-10.core ordering, FA-INV-09) ; [ ] consumers: every surface; [ ] no-claim boundary: hygiene only, no new law.

TESTS: crates/fa-journal/tests/policy.rs and genesis.rs; fa-cli binary tests for D8/D9 exits.

title: `fa verify accumulator` must detect post-checkpoint rewrites and retirements of journal vertices (it rebuilds from historical snapshots and is blind to later in-place changes)
description:
WHY (verified at e606b46): `verify_accumulator` rebuilds each AccumulatorState from `Journal::read(…, Some(st.through_seq))` (crates/fa-notary/src/state.rs:518), i.e. `vertices_at(through_seq)`; the substrate returns the version visible at that sequence (frankengraphdb crates/fgdb/src/lib.rs:4441-4448). A later write that replaces an Entry vertex's payload property (with recomputed digests) or retires the vertex is therefore invisible to verification, while trial balances at head use the altered data. The kernel never writes such versions (payload immutability, FA-INV-02), so this is exactly the adversary tamper evidence exists for (a privileged process or a second writer with the book keys). Only a new `checkpoint` (prefix-extension check at head) or the maintainer's delta guard would notice. The README says verification "recompute[s] the stored chain from the journal" — true only for the historical view.

WHAT: verification also reads the head view of every leaf vertex in the checkpointed prefix and requires: not retired, payload bytes and _fa_digest at head equal the checkpointed record digest, no later version of a payload property (use the substrate's version history if exposed; otherwise compare head vs at-seq bytes); a mismatch is exit 8 with a finding naming the vertex and the first differing sequence. Cost is O(prefix) per verify — state it in the output and in operation_costs.toml (fa-i5s). Add the same head-vs-historical check to `fa verify registers` input selection.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: clean books verify; [ ] planted negatives (real storage writes through the substrate API in a test, bypassing Folio): rewrite an entry payload with recomputed digests after a checkpoint → exit 8; retire an entry vertex → exit 8; rewrite a Leg mirror only → caught by INV-16 check (fa-avx), not this one; [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-14.consistency strengthened) ; [ ] consumers: fa-70o, auditors, fa-verify bundles (the bundle path must carry the same guarantee); [ ] no-claim boundary: detects rewrites inside the book directory; a wholesale replacement of the directory is detected only by witnessed checkpoints (fa-l3c).

TESTS: crates/fa-cli/tests/notary.rs with the substrate write performed by a test helper, transcripts logged.

title: Unit identity: reopening a book must reconcile the journaled Unit vertices with the binary's unit registry and refuse on mismatch; registry rows are id-stable; rendering never panics on an unknown unit
description:
WHY (verified at e606b46): plan §4.4 "A UnitId is immutable, scale included … historical payloads are never rewritten or reinterpreted". Genesis writes Unit vertices with their UNIT_ID (crates/fa-journal/src/genesis.rs:463-479), but `Book::open_dir` rebuilds the unit table from the binary's embedded registries/units.toml (crates/fa/src/book.rs:446 `fa_money::UnitRegistry::embedded()`) and never reads back or compares the journaled rows. Amounts store `unit_id: u32`; if a later binary inserts or reorders a row in units.toml, every stored mantissa is silently reinterpreted under a different unit/scale (e.g. 100 KWD read as 100 BTC), and `Amount::render` panics on an id it does not know (crates/fa-money/src/amount.rs:289). Nothing guards this today.

WHAT: (1) on open (dir and memory books), read every journaled Unit vertex and compare (id, code, kind, scale, rounding_default) with the binary's registry: equal ⇒ proceed; binary has extra later rows ⇒ proceed (additive-minor); any id whose code/scale differs, or a journaled id the binary lacks ⇒ refuse open with exit 5 and `fa doctor` guidance (never "best effort"). (2) fa-registry test: units.toml ids are explicit, unique, never reused, append-only against a pinned fixture (removing/reordering a row fails). (3) `render` returns a typed error for an unknown unit; the CLI maps it to exit 5. (4) The book's journaled unit table becomes the runtime source; the binary's table is only the admission set for NEW units (unit evolution itself is fa-thp).

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: reopen with the same binary works; a binary with an added unit opens old books; [ ] planted negatives: a fixture book whose journaled USD id is re-mapped in a patched registry → open refused exit 5 naming the unit; render of an unknown id → typed error, no panic; [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-02.unit-version activation precondition, FA-INV-06) ; [ ] consumers: fa-thp, every reader; [ ] no-claim boundary: does not implement redenomination or scale change (fa-thp).

TESTS: fa facade reopen tests over a persisted fixture book (real directory); fa-registry append-only test; fa-cli binary test for exit 5 with the error event logged.

title: Make unit evolution, signs, overflow, and FX residual laws mutually consistent
description:
References: §§4.4, 5.2, 6.1/6.4/6.7, Appendix A/F (lines 325, 395, 443, 455, 467, 1131-1132, 1145-1146, 1328, 1333).
1. Amount stores only unit_id and i128 mantissa. §4.4 allows changing that unit's scale and rescaling every stored mantissa, contradicting immutable entries and digests. Example: mantissa 100 means 1 at scale 2 and 0.1 at scale 3. Use immutable unit-version identity with a named conversion/migration law; never silently reinterpret or rewrite historical payloads. Distinguish precision changes from economic redenomination.
2. Entry legs have both Debit/Credit and signed i128 without a nonnegative-leg rule. Reversal wording says exact negation without deciding side swap vs signed storno. Negative legs can undermine per-side amount limits and produce two representations of the same posting. Define one canonical sign convention and boundary behavior, including i128::MIN.
3. Bounded checked i128 amounts are not an unrestricted ordered abelian group: MAX+1 and -MIN fail. Proofs/metamorphics need representability hypotheses or an unbounded reference domain; summation policy must define intermediate overflow and register cumulative totals.
4. FX residual encoding is incomplete: EUR debit 1 minor unit + debit 1 = credit 2; at rate 1/2 under HalfUp, USD base debits 1+1 != credit 1. Adding one USD credit residual fixes base balance but violates USD per-unit balance. Define lawful base-only valuation/residual effects or a complete balanced construction, including remeasurement and historical-cost release, without inventing funds or weakening FA-INV-01.
Acceptance must include these exact examples, inverse/cross-rate scale boundaries, negative refunds/allocations and both per-unit/base validation. W1/W2/W7, G0.
notes:
Addressed in ff3b6eb: §4.4 immutable unit versions (USD@2 -> USD@4 via ScaleConversion law + Redenomination record; historical mantissas never reinterpreted), non-negative mantissas with side swap (no storno; i128::MIN unreachable), bounded register accumulators; §6.1 bounded abelian group with representability hypothesis and independent reference arithmetic; §5.2 valuation residual absorbed by a designated leg with the exact EUR 0.01+0.01/0.02 @ 1/2 HalfUp counterexample, conversion-account pairing for realized FX, revaluation through Valuation contra leaves; §6.5 lot laws. Left open for re-review.

title: fad binds each session to an authenticated principal and presented capability token; `--as`/`--grant` refused on the daemon path; the embedded owner posture is explicit and labelled in every envelope
description:
WHY: plan §15.3 has `fa` auto-route to `fad`, the daemon that owns the writer lease; §14.2 makes authority current-policy-at-commit. At e606b46 fad's `Server::handle` passes the client's raw argv into `cli::run` (crates/fad/src/lib.rs:194-216), so whatever `--as`/`--grant` the client typed becomes the capability; the Unix socket at `<dir>/fad.sock` is bound with no peer-credential check (crates/fad/src/main.rs:161-163). Anyone who can connect to the socket acts as any principal with any op. The `fa capabilities` text claims the opposite (crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:1225).

WHAT:
1. Session handshake on connect: the client sends `{token_commitment, proof}` (from `--token <file>` or `FA_TOKEN`); fad checks SO_PEERCRED uid against the book directory owner policy (registry row: `daemon.allowed_uids = owner|group|list`), verifies the token against the journaled issuance (fa-v62) and binds `(principal, commitment)` for the connection's lifetime; every request on the connection runs under it. Revocation/expiry are re-checked at each commit (kernel witness), and at stream re-admission for long reads (§14.2 "Streams explicitly choose … re-admission").
2. On the daemon path `--as` and `--grant` are refused (exit 7, FA-REF code with fix "present a token: fa cap issue … then --token <file>"), never silently ignored.
3. Embedded posture (no daemon): `--as/--grant` remain for the book-key holder only, through fa-v62's explicit OwnerPosture; the robot envelope gains `authority: {posture: embedded-owner|session, principal, commitment|null}` on every event so no consumer mistakes a self-asserted identity for an authenticated one (robot-schema pin bump, additive-minor).
4. fa-mcp hosted by fad (fa-z5u) inherits this binding: an MCP session is a fad session with the server's launch token.
5. `fa doctor` (fa-12x) reports the posture and warns when an embedded-owner process writes to a book a daemon serves.

ACCEPTANCE:
[ ] positive: two clients of one fad with different tokens are attributed to different principals in the journal (PREPARED_BY / principal_ref), and SoD refuses the second only when it is the same principal;
[ ] planted negatives: a client presenting no token → refused at handshake; a client whose uid is not allowed → refused; a valid token for another book → refused; `--as` on the daemon path → refused exit 7; a token revoked mid-session → the next commit refuses FA-REF-023;
[ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-10.core/current-policy) + lab test over the fad connection loop (crates/fad/src/lab_tests.rs pattern) with chaos;
[ ] consumers: fa-ohe, fa-z5u, every fad user;
[ ] no-claim boundary: Unix peer credentials authenticate a local uid, not a human; human-ness of approvals is a profile/key-custody property (fa-kae).

TESTS: crates/fad/tests/fad.rs (binary, real socket) for each case with frames logged; lab_tests for handshake under chaos; fa-cli tests for `--token`.
