title: Register maintainer must apply the migration visibility predicate exactly as the literal fold does (staged/abandoned runs and pre-opening FullDetail detail are invisible)
description:
WHY (verified at e606b46): the literal fold filters every entry through `fa_journal::migration::visible_at` (crates/fa-registers/src/lib.rs:247); the delta_since maintainer (crates/fa-registers/src/maintainer.rs:270-320) decodes every Entry in the delta and folds it, skipping only Pending/Resolution handling — it never consults migration visibility. For an Open or Abandoned MigrationRun, or FullDetail detail dated before the opening date (plan §8.6, FA-INV-07 migration-disjoint), `Book::advance_registers` publishes cells that include invisible entries, which `verify_period` then reports as drift (exit 8) — a false corruption signal, and a true divergence between maintained and literal folds. Visibility also CHANGES without a new posting to the cell: a Finalize control record makes a whole run visible at once, so the maintainer must treat Finalize/Abandon controls as cell-affecting deltas. No test exercises the maintainer on a Historical or Opening period while a run is open, finalized later, or abandoned. fa-vn4 (WhiteCreek) is landing maintainer changes now (candidate be73b36); coordinate the fix into that series or immediately after it.

WHAT: maintainer folds only entries visible at the delta's commit_seq under the same predicate; a MigrationControl Finalize in the delta re-folds the run's entries into their cells (bounded by the run's chunk manifest, never a full scan); Abandon is a no-op for cells; the metamorphic "rebuild = maintained" test gains migration histories (open → chunks → finalize; open → chunks → abandon; FullDetail with pre-opening detail).

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: maintained cells equal the literal fold at every step of the three histories; [ ] planted negatives: removing the predicate (mutation) makes exactly the new test fail; [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-04.maintainer, FA-INV-07.migration-disjoint) + differential; [ ] consumers: fa-vn4, fa-715, fa-e00; [ ] no-claim boundary: maintainer correctness for native period cells; other register families follow fa-715.

title: Drafts and promotion (A6, doctrine 10 interim posture): intent-log drafts, Agent-profile work lands on a draft, authorized promotion replays to trunk
description:
Background: plan bet A6 says agents work on drafts that cannot touch trunk without authorized promotion; doctrine 10 names the interim posture while substrate branches are not live: intent-log drafts (a DraftSet lifecycle object whose body is the ordered list of intents/proposals, journaled; nothing in it is a trunk entry). fa-llx (MistyPlateau, 2026-10-10) ships the Agent-profile trunk refusal FA-REF-013 whose fix text must cite this bead because the draft path does not exist yet.

Scope: (1) DraftSet lifecycle object (Appendix A): immutable body = book, branch-or-interim marker, owner principal, ordered intents with their dry-run plan certificates and proposal_digests; status projection by LifecycleTransition control entries (Open -> Submitted -> Promoted|Rejected|Abandoned). (2) fa draft new|add|show|submit|promote|abandon with --json and robot envelope events; Agent-profile capabilities may create/add/submit, never promote. (3) Promotion = an authorized Human/System principal replays every intent against trunk inside the normal posting kernel (period law, admissibility, SoD, evidence minimum all re-evaluated at promotion time); any intent whose proposal_digest differs from the draft's recorded digest (because trunk moved: period closed, chart changed, policy epoch changed) is refused with a typed refusal naming the drift, never silently re-approved (FA-INV-10 approval-binds-proposal). (4) Metamorphic test: draft promotion == trunk post (same entries, same digests, same register cells) for model-generated histories; property: a rejected/abandoned draft leaves trunk byte-identical. (5) Oracle: fa-reference models a draft as a list of intents replayed through its own post; differential with planted negatives: Agent promoting (refused), promotion after period close (refused per matrix), drift in proposal_digest (refused), valid promotion (admitted). (6) Switch-over rule registered: when substrate branches land, DraftSet body gains a branch id and promotion becomes a branch merge; the intent-log remains the lineage.

No-claim boundary: green proves promotion re-runs the kernel and refuses drift; it does not prove agents cannot post to trunk through some other surface (that is fa-llx's FA-REF-013 and its tests).

Tests with detailed logging: kernel tests in crates/fa-journal/tests, CLI binary tests, differential floors for each planted negative.

title: Specify public evidence commitments and scope-completeness proofs
description:
References: §§9.1/9.6, 11.11, 13.1-13.3, 15.6, Appendix A/F (lines 560, 580, 704, 745-755, 917, 1188-1194, 1217-1223, 1341).
The MMR is ordered by commit, whereas bundle scopes filter by effective period/account subtree, and retroactive entries make matching records noncontiguous. Inclusion proofs prove supplied leaves belong; they do not prove all matching leaves were supplied. Appendix A contains inclusion_paths but no range/selection-completeness proof, while the CPA workflow says fa-verify confirms a complete FY extract. A producer can omit one matching entry and all retained membership proofs still verify.
Define a sound supported proof mode (e.g. verify the full relevant prefix and selection or an authenticated predicate index bound to the same checkpoint), exact scope/known-at/auth intersection, missing-entry negative vectors, and accurate costs. Do not label membership_only as complete.
Document Oid uses the substrate's keyed identity (fgdb-crypto/src/lib.rs:80-97). A verifier with only public bundle/root cannot recompute it without K_oid. ImportReceipt.digest_at_receipt could provide a public binding, but its algorithm/domain and authenticated binding to Document Oid, kind, bytes and length are not specified. Require an explicit public body commitment chain without disclosing the storage key.
Whole-document hash alone also cannot verify arbitrary disclosed byte ranges against the original redacted document. Define chunk commitments or weaken the redaction proof scope honestly. Specify signature schemes, public trust anchors, key rotation and signed transcript; the std-only verifier budget must cover these implementations.
RFC scope reference: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9162.html . W4/W9, G0/G1.
The canonical Entry deliberately excludes its creating MarkerRef/recorded time. An MMR leaf of only Entry bytes plus a checkpoint's aggregate commit_seq does not authenticate the per-entry commit sequence/HLC, especially when one commit has many leaves. Specify a domain-separated leaf envelope binding record kind, book/branch, creating marker/sequence, and within-commit ordinal, with canonical ordering and a proof of the sequence-to-prefix boundary used by historical selection.
notes: Addressed in ff3b6eb: §13.2 LeafEnvelope binding kind/coordinate/commit_seq/within-commit ordinal/selection fields; ScopeIndexComplete mode with scope_index_root in every checkpoint and boundary-neighbor proofs (missing-entry negative vectors); §9.1 public doc_commit over a 4 KiB chunk tree (substrate ObjectId is a locator only), redaction at chunk granularity labeled honestly; Ed25519 + TrustAnchorSet + KeyRotation in the std-only verifier budget; §13.1 completeness_scope labels; Appendix A LeafEnvelope/ScopeIndex/TransparencyCheckpoint/Bundle; FA-INV-14 clauses. Left open for re-review.

title: Remove approval and certificate hash cycles before freezing durable schemas
description:
References: §4.2/4.6, §10.1/10.4, Appendix A (plan lines 294-305, 333, 592, 645, 1128-1172, 1200-1223).
Entry BodyDigest excludes only entry_digest and includes approvals. ApprovalRef itself contains approved_digest. §4.6 requires that digest to equal the committed object's digest. Consequently d = H(entry containing approval.approved_digest = d), a cryptographic fixed point rather than a constructible approval flow. RestatementCase similarly embeds approvals and mutable lifecycle status. Attestation and checkpoint signature transcripts also lack explicit exclusions of the signatures and signed-digest fields.
Certificate/output references have a related missing contract: Finding contains certificate_oid and the certificate contains output_digest of the result; bundles contain report certificates; Origin::Intent contains plan_certificate_oid. Without a distinct semantic output body, hashing can become cyclic or depend on runtime IDs/approvals and make Canon's byte-for-byte replay claim impossible.
Required repair: an explicit acyclic identity/transcript graph separating immutable proposal digest, approvals/signatures, committed envelope digest, and certified semantic output. Bind approvals to complete effects, book, target coordinate and policy epoch; require reapproval if promotion replays materially different effects. Enumerate ordered construction and digest tags for every signed/certified type. Negative acceptance: change one leg after approval must fail, while adding the first valid approval must be constructible without finding a hash fixed point. W1/W3/W4, G0.
notes:
Addressed in ff3b6eb: §4.6 acyclic identity graph (EntryProposal -> proposal_digest -> plan certificate -> Approvals binding proposal_digest+effects_digest+coordinate+policy epoch -> envelope entry_digest); Appendix A Entry/Approval/Attestation/Checkpoint transcripts exclude signatures/self-digests; normative construction order added; RestatementCase split into immutable body + projection with Approval objects; negative acceptance stated (leg change after approval => digest mismatch refusal; first approval needs no fixed point). Left open for re-review.
2026-10-10 CobaltGull: code consequences landed in fa-model/fa-journal: (1) plan_certificate_oid moved out of the proposal into the envelope (entry_digest = H(domain ‖ proposal_digest ‖ opt(plan_cert) ‖ approvals)); test envelope_fields_change_the_entry_digest_but_not_the_proposal_digest. (2) Idempotency: same key + different content refuses FA-REF-032 exit 6 on both the retry and race-recovery paths (RubyMoose 2739 / WhiteCreek 2730); tests identical_retry_is_recorded_and_a_changed_retry_is_a_conflict + CLI test. (3) Erasable sealing is deterministic under the key (salt/nonce KDF-derived) so identical retries compare equal; WhiteCreek carries the Appendix A row in their patch. (4) fa:entry:v1 is positional schema 1.0: the first additive field needs a minor bump + length-delimited extension block (WhiteCreek 2734) — not yet implemented; lands with the first schema patch that needs it.
2026-10-10 CobaltGull: schema-review.patch (RubyMoose/WhiteCreek) APPLIED to the plan text; code parity, row by row — NOT YET ADMITTED by fa:entry:v1 as encoded: effective_date: Option<DateDay> (code: DateDay on every entry incl. controls); Disposition::Posts { source_ordinals } (code: posted_legs); settles.target_leg: EntryTarget (code: EntryRef); ControlPayload::ReservationRelease (absent); ProposalRef/EffectManifest/IntentOutcome objects (absent; no vid(IntentOutcome) yet, refusals are not durable); Certificate resolved_sequence/resolution_frontier/instant_resolution and DocumentStub proof grammar (no certificate/document code yet). ADMITTED: FA-INV-09 semantic-request equivalence (EntryPayload::semantic_digest, FA-REF-032/033). Each row lands with its slice via the minor-version + extension-block mechanism (msg 2734); the live codec is positional schema 1.0.

title: Bind commit authorization and audit delivery to explicit current policy
description:
References: §§5.1/5.10, 9.7, 14.2-14.4, Appendix A/G/H (lines 375-386, 435, 584, 779-787, 1224-1225, 1365-1375, 1399).
Plan has initial admission and commit-time SoD but no explicit current-policy witness for revocation/expiry between dry run and commit, or for reads pinned before revocation. known_at should select accounting history without resurrecting revoked access. Define security epoch, current authority evaluation, approval authority expiry/revocation policy and fail-closed boundaries.
daily_total and per-entry amount ceilings require a precise measure (gross debit, credit, absolute per-leg, per-unit), day/time-zone source, shared principal/token scope and serializable budget debit. Net of balanced entries is always zero. Attenuation/issuance must not reset a principal ceiling. No operation-cost row prices those stateful checks.
Every external-profile read must be completely logged, but Appendix G declares balance/report/bundle reads 0 writes. Define durable access recording before protected bytes escape, stream/cancellation/failure semantics, daemon authority for read-only callers, and avoidance of recursive log reads. Price the real transaction/barrier or name a distinct admitted audit path.
Account-subtree/dimension caveats and full immutable Entry payloads conflict when one entry crosses an authorized and unauthorized account: define whole-entry admission, redacted/partial-view representation and proof scope, or refuse before fetching; do not return the full other-account leg or silently describe a partial fold as whole-book.
Acceptance: revoke after plan, historical read using revoked token, two simultaneous daily-budget posts, token attenuation, crash before/after first protected output byte, and split-scope balanced entry. W2/Steward/W5, G0/G1.
The ordering of ADMIT→RESOLVE→CANON also needs explicit post-evaluation authorization: a typed event does not yet have its generated accounts/dimensions/amounts at step 1. Safely admit explicit inputs, run under restricted capabilities, then validate every generated effect and current caveat before commit. Initial authorization of the verb alone is insufficient.
notes:
Addressed in ff3b6eb: §5.1 step 5 post-evaluation authorization of rule-generated legs; §14.2 closed ops vocabulary, current-policy witness at commit (PlanInvalidated{CapabilityRevoked}), historical selectors never resurrect authority, ceiling measure (per-leg mantissa; daily gross debits per root issuance; day from TimeEvidence) via a UsageCell, whole-entry visibility with partial_view; §9.7 AccessEvent committed before the first protected byte and priced as an Appendix G row; FA-INV-10 clauses. title: Docket slice 2: custody chains, ImportRun control records with receipt hashes, external document storage behind public commitments with verified reads, redaction contracts as derived objects, retention holds blocking erasure and expiry
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-10, CobaltGull): Docket's first slice (fa-lp6) delivers content-addressed documents, chunk-Merkle commitments, evidence minimums and `EVIDENCED_BY`; fa-journal/src/evidence.rs lists custody, import receipts, bank lines, external storage and redaction as "later slices". Plan §9 and W4 require them before Gate G2 ("documents, custody, attestations, balance assertions"). fa-v74 (subject keys) and fa-646 (intake pipeline) touch adjacent ground; fa-j9t is the spec-side contract bead. This bead is the code.

WHAT:
1. Custody chain: every document carries an immutable `Custody` lineage (received-from principal/system, received-at CommitSeq, transfer events as journaled objects), queryable as `fa document custody <oid>`; a document cannot be cited by an entry unless its custody chain is complete to a registered intake source.
2. Import receipts: `ImportRun` as a control record (legs = []) with the source descriptor, byte count, document count, the Merkle root over the imported documents' oids, and a receipt hash the external party can keep; `fa import receipt <run>`; receipts are what fa-ff6 and fa-646 must produce.
3. External document storage: documents above the inline threshold store bytes outside the journal under a registered store descriptor with the public commitment (chunk-tree root) inline; reads verify the commitment on every access; a missing external blob is a typed refusal (exit 5, foundation/I-O) and never a silent null; the plan's "public commitments" let a bundle prove a document without shipping it.
4. Redaction contracts: `redaction = <contract>` capability caveat; a redacted view of a document is a derived object with its own commitment and lineage to the original; redaction never changes an amount or an entry (erasure-leaves-amounts-intact oracle); subject-key erasure (fa-v74) composes with this.
5. Retention holds: `RetentionHold` control records that block erasure cuts and expiry sweeps for the held subjects; releases are journaled.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: an import run of N documents produces a receipt whose root recomputes from the oids; an external document reads back byte-identically with the commitment verified; a redacted view omits the field and keeps the entry's amounts; a hold blocks an erasure cut with a refusal naming the hold; [ ] planted negatives: a tampered external blob is refused on read (exit 8); a document without custody cannot be cited (refusal names the missing link); an erasure cut under a hold is refused; [ ] proof class: invariant (commitments, lineage) + differential (fa-reference naive custody/receipt model); [ ] consumers: fa-ff6, fa-646, fa-v74, bundles (A3), G2; [ ] no-claim boundary: receipts prove what was imported, not that the source was truthful.

TESTS: kernel tests in fa-journal/tests with oids and roots logged, CLI binary tests, differential floors per planted negative.

title: Bind every verdict to an exact tree: per-step verdict manifests keyed by tree hash (a split run is one verdict iff every step PASSed on that tree), scripts/local_proof.sh + merge_train.sh + br_sync.sh adopted from the substrate, verdicts as git notes; bead closes cite a manifest id
description:
WHY: AGENTS.md "A green scripts/check.sh in a dirty tree is not a verdict"; local_proof.sh "runs scripts/check.sh against the exact committed tree, refuses a dirty worktree, and writes a manifest binding the verdict to that commit and tree hash"; merge_train.sh is "the only path from staging to main". At e606b46 none of local_proof.sh, merge_train.sh, br_sync.sh, check-forbidden-deps.sh exist, there are no git notes refs, and the last literal single check.sh exit 0 is a7203b82 (2026-10-10 22:24), 45 commits before the tip; the tip has clippy + tests on an equivalent tree but no check.sh run. Because rch's daemon queue cap (300 s) and 1800/3600/7200 s kill limits routinely leave steps UNRUN, the swarm has closed beads on stitched runs (a full run with 13 PASS / 2 UNRUN plus a separate `--quick` run at the same tree, e.g. 3a4349f; commit 5de0c4b itself notes "their concatenation is not a new all-fifteen-step verdict"). The doctrine is right; the tooling to satisfy it honestly under a saturated fleet is missing, which is what pushes people into stitching.

WHAT (the ambitious, honest fix): (1) check.sh writes a per-step verdict record `{step, status PASS|FAIL|UNRUN, tree_hash, toolchain, worker, started, finished, log_digest}` to a manifest; (2) `scripts/local_proof.sh <commit>` refuses a dirty tree, runs only the steps not already PASSed for that exact tree hash and toolchain, and emits a final verdict manifest iff every registered step has a PASS record for that tree — so a split run IS one verdict by construction, with no human stitching; any FAIL for that tree invalidates the manifest; (3) manifests stored as git notes under refs/notes/fa-verdict keyed by commit, and mirrored to origin; (4) `scripts/merge_train.sh run` merges staging into a private clone, requires a verdict manifest for the exact resulting tree, and fast-forwards main only then (gives the owner a verdict to merge PRs by); (5) `scripts/br_sync.sh <ids…>` flushes and verifies the exact bead set before staging JSONL (AGENTS.md landing step 4); (6) bead-close helper refuses to close without citing a manifest id whose tree contains the bead's landing commit; (7) check.sh's registry step stops being a grep (fa-szi replaces it) and forbidden-deps gains the cargo tree --invert posture-confinement check (§18.4).

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: a run split across two workers (one step UNRUN on the first) completes on the second and produces one manifest for that tree; [ ] planted negatives: a FAIL recorded for the tree blocks the manifest; a dirty tree is refused; a manifest for tree A cannot close a bead landed in tree B; [ ] proof class: gate (verdict contract) ; [ ] consumers: every landing, the owner's staging→main merges, bead closes; [ ] no-claim boundary: binds verdicts to trees; does not make a weak step strong.

TESTS: scripts/tests/ shell tests with fixture repos for each case; shellcheck clean.

title: Capability issuance as journaled control + holder-bound capability tokens + kernel verification of the presented token; profiles and caveats registry (capability_caveats.toml)
description:
WHY: plan §14.2 says caveats are conjunctive and attenuable only and "issuance and revocation are journaled control entries"; §14.4 registers ten profile templates (Agent, Preparer, Approver, Controller, Auditor, Regulator/Examiner, Investigator, Receiver/Trustee, Production, Witness); Appendix A has `ControlPayload::CapabilityEvent { commitment, kind: Issue | Revoke | Attenuate, caveats_digest }`. At e606b46 revocation is journaled (fa-llx e97746b, FA-REF-023) and witnessed on writes (fa-bcd), but there is no issuance: every capability is constructed in-process from argv by `Capability::embedded` (crates/fa-policy/src/capability.rs:237-247) and the kernel checks only that the presented value is not revoked (crates/fa-journal/src/policy.rs:714). Profiles implemented: Human/Agent/System only (capability.rs:56). `registries/capability_caveats.toml` does not exist. So there is nothing an operator can hand an agent that the kernel will verify, and nothing that makes "the holder of this token is principal P with ops O" true by construction. WHAT: 0. Consume before building (doctrine 10, AGENTS.md "Never a copy of substrate code"): first evaluate FrankenGraphDB's live Warden permit/policy types (`fgdb-warden`, `fgdb-policy`; plan §2.1 "Policy/permit types live") and asupersync's macaroons/authenticated types (plan §2.2) as the token format and attenuation algebra; record the decision (adopt, or why not) as an Appendix H row update (R-WARDEN) in the same change. Build an FA-level token only for what those types cannot express, and keep the accounting caveat vocabulary owned here. 1. `registries/capability_caveats.toml`: the closed `ops` vocabulary (21 names, already `fa-policy/src/op.rs:11-59` — the registry becomes the source and the code is checked against it), the caveat vocabulary of §14.2 with per-caveat status live|dormant (live today: ops, per-leg ceilings, books, expires_at; others dormant naming their bead), and the ten profile templates as data (ops ceilings, required caveats such as Agent ⇒ branch-confined + requires_dry_run once fa-we7/fa-s7x land). fa-registry reader + parity test vs op.rs. 2. `IssueCapability` control (Appendix A CapabilityEvent{Issue}): issued by a principal holding `issue_capability`, under SoD for `IssueCapability(ops ∋ restate)` (sod_policy.toml row), body = {holder principal, profile, caveats (sorted, tag-coded like Capability v2), expires_at, parent commitment for attenuation}, commitment = BLAKE3 over the canonical body; journaled, immutable; a Capability metadata vertex keyed by commitment (identity-derived vid) is the point-read witness the kernel checks at commit (exists, not revoked, not expired, holder matches session principal). 3. Capability token = the canonical body + a holder key binding (the holder's public key, Ed25519 via fa-l3c's signer once landed; until then a 32-byte secret whose hash is in the body), stored in a 0600 token file like DatabaseKeys. Attenuation produces a child body whose caveats ⊆ parent's and whose daily_total root is the parent's root issuance (§14.2 "attenuation never resets a ceiling"). 4. Kernel: `admit` takes a `PresentedCapability { commitment, proof }`, point-reads the Capability vertex, verifies proof-of-possession, and derives the effective caveats from the JOURNALED body — never from a caller-built struct. The embedded owner posture keeps `Capability::embedded` but only behind an explicit `OwnerPosture` constructor that requires the book key file and is labelled in every outcome (`authority.posture = "embedded-owner"`), so tests and single-user CLI keep working and the label makes the trust boundary visible. 5. CLI: `fa cap issue --holder

--profile [--caveat k=v]... --out `, `fa cap list|show [--json]`, (revoke is fa-1d6 and reuses the commitment); robot events `capability_issued`, `capability`; verbs.toml + MCP parity (issue is NOT exposed to Agent-profile MCP sessions). 6. fa-reference: naive issuance/attenuation/expiry/revocation model; differential over generated issue/attenuate/revoke/use histories. ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: a Controller issues an Agent token; a post presented with it on trunk is refused FA-REF-013; a read with it succeeds; an attenuated child with a smaller per-leg ceiling refuses a leg above it; issuance is visible in `fa cap list --json` with the issuing control entry's EntryRef; [ ] planted negatives (one check each): forged body (caveats edited after issuance) → commitment mismatch refusal; valid body, wrong proof-of-possession → refused; attenuation widening an op → refused at issuance; issuance by a principal lacking issue_capability → FA-REF-012; IssueCapability with ops ∋ restate without the SoD approval → FA-REF-008; expired token → refused at the admission point (expires_at against TimeEvidence per §14.2 "Expiry admission"); [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-10.core/current-policy over journaled issuance) + differential vs fa-reference; [ ] consumers: fa-r3q, fa-0x0, fa-7dw, fa-ohe, fa-1d6, fa-s7x, fa-z5u, fa-zgn (Auditor profile); [ ] no-claim boundary: tokens prove possession of a journaled grant; key custody of the holder's secret is the operator's responsibility (R-KEY interim). TESTS: fa-policy unit tests for attenuation algebra (property tests: caveats only narrow, ceilings never reset); fa-journal kernel tests for every negative; fa-cli binary tests for issue/list/show with robot transcripts logged; fa-reference differential with the seed printed.

title: Subject keys: per-Party erasable-field keys held outside the journal (R-KEY), managed by fad, with Party objects; ErasureCut switch-over from the typed refusal
description:
Background: fa-lp6 (TopazOsprey, 2026-10-10) ships Erasable<T> fields with subject_ref but every key is the book key, and ErasureCut is a typed refusal (FA-REF-088) citing plan 8.5 / Appendix H R-ERASE: an FA-level tombstone that leaves plaintext reachable is a prohibited shortcut, so erasure waits for destroyable per-subject keys. The invariant 'redaction or key loss never changes an amount' is proven in fa-lp6 on the real substrate.

Scope: (1) Party objects (vertices, content-addressed, immutable body) as the subjects of erasable fields; (2) a subject-key store OUTSIDE the append-only journal: a keys file owned by fad (writer lease) with per-Party keys, key ids referenced from Erasable<T>.subject_ref, key creation journaled as a control entry naming the key id (never the key), destruction journaled as a typed tombstone naming the key id and the legal basis; (3) fold/read behaviour with a destroyed key: amounts, digests, registers, trial balance unchanged; erased fields render as a typed absence naming the tombstone; retry equivalence per FA-REF-033; (4) ErasureCut control entry (plan 8.5) admitted only with a destroyable key present, SoD row for erasure, refusal rows updated; (5) oracle in fa-reference models key presence; differential plants: erasure with the book key (refused), erasure of a subject with live legal hold (refused), valid erasure (admitted, amounts unchanged), read after destruction (typed absence); (6) CLI: fa party add, fa erase <subject> --basis <code> --yes, fa keys status; MCP parity later.

Depends on fa-lp6 (Erasable fields, SupplementalEvidence) and fa-i8j (fad owns the keys file). No-claim boundary: green proves key destruction removes plaintext reachability through FA's own readers and never changes an amount; it does not claim substrate-level erasure (R-ERASE) or storage-media guarantees.

Testing: real-substrate kernel tests, CLI binary tests with detailed logs, differential floors for each planted negative.

title: Make fa-reference independent where it matters: its own period resolution, period state machine and admissibility table (no calls into fa-time/fa-registry decision code), its own unbounded arithmetic in the application law, an exhaustive Appendix C cell test, and multi-seed differential campaigns
description:
WHY (verified at e606b46): plan §16.2 — "a mismatch is triaged against the spec and never resolved by making the reference imitate the engine"; AGENTS.md — the oracle has "its own limb arithmetic … so a shared arithmetic bug cannot make the differential green". fa-reference calls the kernel's own `periods_for_year`, `resolve_period`, `transition` (fa-time) and `Admissibility::decide` (fa-registry) (crates/fa-reference/src/lib.rs:55-60, :978, :1127, :1562-1567), and its docs say it "mirrors the kernel's law order exactly" (lib.rs:6-11). For period law and admissibility, therefore, the differential proves the kernel is wired to those functions, not that the laws are right — fa-zxm's reversal-period bug survived precisely because both sides omit it. Its application law uses raw i128 (lib.rs:1752-1764, :2608-2618, :2629), contradicting the own-limbs design (it would panic, not refuse, on overflow). title: fa-registers maintainer: incremental delta_since folds with a CAS watermark, RegisterCheckpoint control records with checkpoint cadence as a decision card, rebuild = maintained metamorphic, recovery discards and rebuilds, read paths never serve stale cells, Ripple switch-over rule registered
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-10, CobaltGull): Bet A1 says balances are "materialized incrementally and verifiable by recomputation", W2 names "the fa-registers maintainer over delta_since", and Appendix H registers the interim posture for Ripple views as a FrankenAccounting-level `delta_since` register maintainer. At 96d1918 every fold is a full rescan of the entry stream at a known-at seq (fa-registers/src/lib.rs `fold_period`, `trial_balance_at`); `materialize` writes register vertices and `verify_period` compares, but there is no incremental maintainer, no watermark advance from `delta_since`, no checkpoints, and `delta_since` has 0 hits. This is correct but will not scale, and the recovery rule ("recovery discards and rebuilds") has no code path to exercise.

WHAT:
1. The maintainer: `Registers::advance(&cx, book)` reads the substrate's `delta_since(watermark)` entry stream, folds only the new entries into the register cells (period × account × unit, plus the pending, open-item, availability and per-entity cells as they exist), moves the watermark under CAS inside the same transaction, and is idempotent under crash (re-running from a stale watermark yields identical cells).
2. Checkpoints: a journaled `RegisterCheckpoint` control record (legs = []) naming the watermark and the fold digest per register family; verify-by-fold runs from the last checkpoint or from genesis on demand; the checkpoint cadence is an adaptive decision with a decision card and a pinned fallback (every N entries), per the adaptive-decision contract.
3. Recovery: `fa registers rebuild` discards every register vertex and refolds from genesis (or from a checkpoint whose digest verifies); the rebuilt cells equal the maintained ones (metamorphic `rebuild = maintained`); `fa verify registers` stays green across the rebuild.
4. Reads: the report paths use maintained cells only when their watermark covers the requested known-at and the cells' verify digest matches; otherwise they fold (never a stale answer; the envelope reports which path answered).
5. Switch-over rule: when the substrate's Ripple views land, the maintainer becomes the registered interim's replacement per Appendix H; the rule is recorded in foundation_dependencies.toml.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: after N posts, `advance` moves the watermark by N and the maintained trial balance equals the full fold byte-for-byte; a crash between fold and watermark move (fa-sim crash point) leaves cells that re-advance to the same result; `rebuild` reproduces every cell; [ ] planted negatives: a maintainer mutation that skips one entry class is caught by verify-by-fold; a checkpoint with a forged digest is refused on rebuild; reading maintained cells past their watermark is refused by the read path test; [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-04 register-never-more-authoritative, live) + metamorphic; [ ] consumers: every report path, G1 register verification, fa-sim campaigns; [ ] no-claim boundary: incremental equality is proven on the covered register families only.

TESTS: fa-registers integration tests with watermark and digests logged, fa-sim crash-point campaign for the maintainer, metamorphic rebuild test, CLI binary tests.

title: Statistical audit lane with independent oracles: in-house exact Benford/KS/chi-square procedures checked against frankenscipy fsci-stats (test-only), NumPy-reproducible sampling via franken_numpy fnp-random-core (PCG64DXSM), property suites on frankensim fs-propcheck
description:
WHY: doctrine 12 — a detector's score is `statistical` evidence, never an invariant; an examiner must be able to re-run the numbers in Python. frankenscipy (/data/projects/frankenscipy) has chisquare, power_divergence, kstest/ks_1samp, binomtest and Binomial/Hypergeometric/Poisson/ChiSquared distributions — all f64, so it cannot produce the certified statistic but is an ideal TEST-ONLY checker (fa-lantern dev-dependency; 4 MB lib.rs compile cost noted). franken_numpy's fnp-random-core (366 lines, zero deps, forbid(unsafe)) gives SeedSequence + Pcg64Dxsm bit-compatible with np.random.PCG64DXSM, so a sample drawn from a declared seed is reproducible in Python; the seed is a declared input (no entropy capability, doctrine 3). frankensim's fs-propcheck (zero deps: deterministic property testing with shrinking and seed replay) and fs-rand (seeded streams independent of scheduling) serve the §16.6 property/metamorphic suites and fa-gen.
WHAT: (1) crates/fa-lantern first slice: exact-integer Benford first/second-digit expected counts (rational expectation × n, law-rounded), chi-square and KS statistics over register legs with a certificate; (2) `fa sample random|mus --seed <declared> --size n` over open items/legs using fnp-random-core, output reproducible by a documented NumPy snippet; (3) dev-dependencies: fsci-stats pinned by git rev as the differential oracle for the statistics (tolerance stated as an f64 oracle bound, never applied to amounts); fs-propcheck for property suites; (4) registry rows for the procedures' claim classes.
ACCEPTANCE: [ ] oracle differential passes on fixtures and generated histories; [ ] sample reproducibility test vectors (seed → indices) pinned; [ ] no float in any amount path; [ ] `fa capabilities --json` lists the procedures with claim class statistical. UPSTREAM: frankenscipy — integer/exact-rational entry points for expected counts, or document f64 as oracle-only.
notes:
Upstream issue filed 2026-10-10: https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankenscipy/issues/16 (oracle numerical contract; exact entry points; split lib.rs).

title: Document intake requires a capability and derives the provenance grade from the intake source and principal profile; the caller can never declare `HumanUpload`
description:
WHY: plan §9.3 — every document carries a provenance grade derived from its receipt chain (ThirdPartySigned, Connector, HumanUpload, AgentUpload, Generated); an entry whose only evidence is AgentUpload/Generated is self-sourced and needs a human Reviewed attestation before promotion (FA-INV-05; AGENTS.md "a document you uploaded yourself is graded AgentUpload"). title: fa-intents first slice: typed intents with canonical bytes, Book::plan dry-run returning a Plan with a PlanCertificate, Book::commit(plan) re-validating the bound fields (PlanInvalidated refusals), confirm_plan gating, non-null certificate in the robot envelope
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-10, CobaltGull): Bet A6 says agents work through typed intents with dry-run plans, and plan §19 says the Genesis slice takes "real PostEntry, IntentHeader and Plan types from fa-intents". At 96d1918 `fa::Book` has `post` but no `session/plan/commit`; `plan_certificate` is always `None` (fa-cli main.rs ~1750, fa book.rs ~849); the robot envelope's `certificate` field is emitted as `null`; `confirm_plan` has zero hits. An Agent-profile capability is refused on trunk with a pointer to drafts (fa-s7x), so today an agent cannot post at all. Intents are the laws-layer abstraction (crate layer "laws": pure, stripped Cx) that both drafts (fa-s7x) and Canon (W6) build on, so this slice must exist before either.

WHAT (first real slice, not a prototype):
1. `crates/fa-intents` (laws layer; no I/O, no Cx with capabilities): `IntentHeader { book, branch, principal, capability_ref, idempotency_key, known_at? }`, the intent union for the classes the kernel admits today (PostEntry, Reverse, Reserve, Resolve, Settle, PeriodTransition, DocumentAdd) with Appendix B field names, a canonical byte form (versioned, additive-minor, tag-coded like fa:entry:v1) and `proposal_digest` (which already exists in the kernel; move the single source here).
2. `Book::plan(&cap, intent) -> Plan`: a dry run that runs the full posting pipeline up to but excluding commit (admission, period law, evidence minimum, balance law, limits, SoD) against a snapshot, returning the effects (legs, mirrors it would move, approvals it needs, refusal it would raise) and a `PlanCertificate { proposal_digest, effects_commitment, snapshot_seq, security_policy_epoch, expires_at_seq }`; nothing is written.
3. `Book::commit(&cap, plan)`: re-validates the certificate's bound fields (plan §4.6 line 371: proposal digest, effects commitment, coordinate, policy epoch, current SoD, execution authority) inside the serializable transaction and refuses `PlanInvalidated { reason }` (new FA-REF codes with catalog rows) when any changed; otherwise commits with `plan_certificate` recorded on the entry and emitted in the robot envelope (`certificate` non-null).
4. `confirm_plan`: dangerous verbs (post with post_closed, period close/lock/reopen, resolve voids) require `--yes` or a `--confirm-plan <certificate>` whose digest matches; the refusal names the safe alternative (`--dry-run`).
5. CLI: `fa post --dry-run` emits the plan with its certificate (Agent-profile capabilities imply dry-run once per session, §15); `fa commit --plan <file|digest>`; robot events `plan`, `plan_invalidated`.
6. Oracle: fa-reference models plan = pure evaluation and commit = re-evaluation under the current state; differential plants: a plan invalidated by a concurrent close, by an epoch change, by a revoked capability, by changed legs; a valid plan commits byte-identically to a direct post.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: `fa post --dry-run --json` returns a certificate and writes nothing (journal head unchanged, proven by `fa verify registers` and an entry count); the same plan committed produces the same entry bytes as a direct post (metamorphic test); [ ] planted negatives: each `PlanInvalidated` reason is exercised by a test that changes exactly that bound field between plan and commit; [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-11.core: certificates replayable) + differential; [ ] consumers: fa-s7x drafts (intent-log), fa-canon (intents bound to rule families), fa-cli/fa-mcp dry-run macros, FA-INV-11; [ ] no-claim boundary: a certificate proves what the plan bound, not that the intent was economically correct.

TESTS: fa-intents unit tests for canonical bytes (golden vectors per minor), kernel tests in fa-journal/tests, CLI binary tests for dry-run/commit/confirm_plan, differential floors ≥ 3 per planted reason, all with the proposal digest logged.

title: Resolve special periods, carry-forward folds, and report cutoffs
description:
References: §§4.8, 7.1-7.5, 8.6, 12.1/12.5, 15.6, Appendix A/C/F (lines 349, 475-491, 552, 717, 733, 919, 1181, 1265-1279, 1330).
A date must resolve to exactly one Period, but normal December, adjustment period 13 and closing/opening periods can share civil dates. There is no target-period field on Entry/PostEntry or registered routing rule to disambiguate. Shared calendar identity also needs separation from per-book period state.
The fold boundary is not defined for stock vs flow: FOR PERIOD filters effective dates, while balance-sheet/TB positions require opening balances; §7.5 additionally posts next-year opening balances despite an all-time append-only fold. Simple cash 100 at year end plus a new opening 100 becomes 200 under All unless openings are anchors or an explicit selection law excludes double counting. Closing entries likewise must not zero the income-statement activity reported for the closed year.
§8.6 imports opening trial balance plus optional full legacy history; specify a cut so both cannot be counted twice.
§7.4 defines originally reported as first Closed, while close can include further adjusting entries before publication/lock. Either label this view as first close or persist a ReportPublication fact/certificate; retain AS REPORTED IN for actual filings.
Required examples: Dec 31 normal/adjustment/closing, FY aggregate, Jan opening, pre/post-close P&L and BS, known-at retrospective correction, multi-book shared calendar with independent status, migration opening+detail. Special-period reference: https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_S4HANA_ON-PREMISE/651d8af3ea974ad1a4d74449122c620e/2252d7531a4d424de10000000a174cb4.html . W1/W3/W7/W9, G0.
Appendix C refuses PriorPeriodAdjustment in Open/SoftClosed, although §8.1 defines it as an opening-retained-earnings adjustment. Decide whether it posts into the current open period while referring to historical error periods, or whether its class name means a different operation; do not force a current-period correction into a closed/locked target.
notes:
Addressed in ff3b6eb: §7.3 effective_period discriminator (special periods must be named; class-restricted); §4.1 Period key per book with shared calendar; §7.5 stock-vs-flow rule (flow lines filter by period, stock lines fold EFFECTIVE <= end), income statements exclude Closing, no opening-balance entries, incremental reclose + nominal-zero; §8.6 migration-disjoint modes; §7.4/§12.5 AS ORIGINALLY REPORTED anchored to StatementIssuance; Appendix C PriorPeriodAdjustment row posts in the current open period with relates_to. title: Solvency, lookback and distribution procedures (plan §11.5–11.6): solvency.balance_sheet_test/cash_flow_test, lookback.preferences with computed §547(c) defenses, lookback.fraudulent_transfer, ponzi.net_investment, distribution.rising_tide/pro_rata, damages.but_for over scenario scratch books
description:

Huber), distribution.pro_rata (Cunningham v. Brown) with investor cohorts and clawback schedules; damages.but_for = statements on a scenario scratch book (fa-s7x) minus trunk, certified (fa-cqk).

title: Never-silent-fail on panic: install a panic hook in fa, fad and fa-mcp that emits exactly one robot `error` event (exit 5, refusal_id, class "internal") instead of exit 101 with no event
description:
WHY: plan §15.3 "every non-zero exit emits exactly one error event carrying refusal_id, exit, and class, which is what the never-silent-fail regression test asserts"; exit code 1 is never emitted and Rust's panic exit is 101. At e606b46 there is no panic hook (Teller audit): a panic in the substrate or a dependency exits 101 with no error event, breaking the robot contract and the exit-code dictionary. Surface code has no unwrap/expect, but the substrate and foundations can still panic.

WHAT: a panic hook (std::panic::set_hook) in each binary's main that writes one `error` event (stdout when --json, stderr text otherwise), maps to exit 5 with class "internal" and refusal_id, and includes the panic location; fad keeps serving other connections where the region model allows (a panic inside one request's region is that request's error, not the daemon's death) — verify with asupersync's region semantics; a test binary feature `fa-test-panic` (dev-only, compiled out of release) triggers a panic to test it.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: forced panic → exit 5 + one error event; [ ] planted negative: removing the hook fails the test; [ ] proof class: e2e; [ ] consumers: agents, fa-fs0; [ ] no-claim boundary: process-level reporting; aborts (OOM kill) cannot be reported.

TESTS: fa-cli/fad/fa-mcp binary tests.

title: fa-mcp containment: tool arguments that name host filesystem paths (document/intent/plan/chart inputs, plan_out output) require an explicit launch filesystem root or are refused; inline/forwarded-stdin forms are the MCP path
description:
WHY (TopazOsprey 4185, WhiteCreek 4184, 2026-10-11): after fa-23r a launch-bound fa-mcp fixes identity, authority, the book and its keys, but path arguments still resolve against the server process's working directory on the host: fa_evidence_import_document.file, fa_post_post/reserve/resolve.intent_file and fa_chart_import_chart.file read any file the server's OS user can read; fa_time_period_transition.plan reads a plan file; plan_out writes one anywhere the user can write. An agent holding read+post can therefore import arbitrary host files as documents or write files outside the book. fa-23r explicitly does NOT claim filesystem confinement.

WHAT:
1. In the MCP posture the inline / forwarded-stdin forms (intent, text, chart) are the positive path.
2. A path argument is refused with a structured error whose fix names the inline form, unless the launch configuration grants an explicit filesystem root (--files <dir>); paths are then resolved under that root with no .., symlink or absolute escape.
3. plan_out and plan work only under that root.
4. Audit every tool, resource and macro (fa-z5u's macros included) that accepts a path.
5. Planted negatives: absolute path, .. escape, symlink escape, and a path given without the root; positive: inline forms and an in-root path.

ACCEPTANCE: positive observable = an e2e stdio session launched with --files <dir> imports a document from under the root and the same call with a path outside it is refused with the structured error; planted negatives as in WHAT 5 each reaching exactly one check; proof class = e2e + unit on the resolver; consumers = every MCP host, fa-z5u, fa-ohe; no-claim boundary = this confines path arguments only; it is not a sandbox for the server process and does not authenticate the operator (fa-v62/fa-r3q).

title: Owner-project survey and adoption decisions (2026-10-10): what each of the owner's 47 Rust projects can contribute to FrankenAccounting, the rulings that govern adoption, and the upstream issues filed
description:
PURPOSE: the durable record of the 2026-10-10 survey of every Rust project written by the owner (47 projects, local checkouts under /data/projects and GitHub Dicklesworthstone), evaluated for applicability, utility and accretion to FrankenAccounting, plus the owner rulings that govern adoption. Read this before proposing any dependency; do not re-survey.

OWNER RULINGS (binding, recorded in AGENTS.md doctrine 1 and README):
1. The closed dependency universe excludes THIRD-PARTY crates only. Every Rust project written by the owner — Franken-named or not (e.g. fastapi_rust) — is an admissible foundation, pinned by git rev, with its transitive closure confined by deny.toml wrapper allowlists exactly like asupersync/frankengraphdb/fnx/fastmcp-rust. First-party code still never imports serde, tokio, chrono, decimal crates, arrow or SQLite bindings directly.
2. Upstream changes are fine: file GitHub issues with the requests (nine filed, listed below).
3. Adoption follows a concrete consumer slice (plan rule): each adoption bead lands the pin in the same change as the first consuming code.

METHOD: four read-only explorer passes (no builds), each reading README/plan/architecture headers, root Cargo manifests, crate counts, .rs counts, #[test] counts, status notes and last commit dates; verdicts are tied to file paths. Present-tense READMEs about planned systems were not accepted as evidence.

ADOPT NOW (beads): franken_markdown → fa-cet (deterministic PDF/A-2b, HTML, SVG statements; std-only engine fmd-font/fmd-math with clap/wasm/asupersync optional; ~4.5k tests; src/pdfa.rs, src/diff.rs semantic diff, src/diagrams.rs flowcharts; crates.io v0.5.0; numeric table alignment/footing to be verified by fixture first). frankensympy → fa-pri (fsym-bigint/fsym-rational: normalised exact rationals, cross-cancelled composition, metered arithmetic; local snapshot has no .git — pin upstream f449ab0; its own plan calls the exact substrate an open decision; today it wraps num-bigint/num-rational with serde derives — allowlisted as foundation transitives).

ADOPT LATER OR TEST-ONLY (beads): frankenscipy fsci-stats → fa-vpk (chisquare, power_divergence, kstest/ks_1samp, binomtest, Binomial/Hypergeometric/Poisson/ChiSquared; f64 only, so test-only oracle; 4 MB lib.rs; nightly CI not green per its README). franken_numpy fnp-random-core → fa-vpk (366 lines, zero deps, forbid(unsafe); SeedSequence + Pcg64Dxsm bit-compatible with np.random.PCG64DXSM for seed-declared reproducible audit sampling; bit-exactness is the README's claim, 5 tests in the core crate). frankensim fs-propcheck / fs-rand / fs-blake3 → fa-vpk (zero-dep property testing with shrinking and seed replay; seeded streams; a test-time BLAKE3 cross-check; frankensim has no local .git — pin upstream; its README says not yet an integrated end-user application; skip fs-eproc (asupersync covers it), fs-ledger (frankensqlite), fs-qty (no money)). frankengit fgit-deflate → fa-646 (std-only bounded streaming zlib/DEFLATE, 3,865 LOC, 41 tests, for PDF FlateDecode and ZIP-based XBRL/SAF-T packages; the rest of frankengit (234 third-party packages, fgit-crypto with ed25519-dalek) is not needed; its constellation.lock pattern is already plan §2.6). franken_lean fln check-olean → fa-uqq (zero external crates; elaborator accepts only 25 of 2,961 upstream elab tests so it cannot compile our .lean, but check-olean accepted all 2,433 stdlib modules — a second kernel over anchors compiled by upstream Lean; fln-bignum uses Lean number semantics, wrong for money). franken_ocr focr and franken_whisper fw robot → fa-646 (external processes only: both link frankensqlite and other closures; OCR has 19.3% character error rate on its own corpus so output is advisory, never an amount source; whisper NDJSON transcripts with diarization; models download separately 1.6 GB + 0.49 GB). hedge_fund_data_tool → fa-646 after upstream extraction (deterministic PDF text-layer extraction crates/hfdt-sources/src/extract.rs pdf_text_to_text, no OCR; hfdt-pdf-crypto AES-256 empty-password PDFs with deps aes+sha2 only; hfdt-tables cells-as-evidence; hfdt-accounting-quality statement-level procedures; inline-XBRL reader only; no Benford; proprietary license; carries chrono/serde today). flywheel_connectors → fa-ff6 (separate supervised process: fwc → fcp-host → connector subprocesses over stdio/JSON-RPC; connectors/plaid transactions_sync and accounts_balance_get, snowflake sql.write/sql.query, bigquery, s3, stripe, postgresql; cannot be linked: tokio/hyper/reqwest/chrono in fcp-async-core). franken_alignment → fa-s30 (GitHub only; reference model, zero external crates, nightly-2026-09-07; one-shot permits bound to immutable payloads, conserved rights, authority-graph dominators/min-cuts for separation of duties, judgment caching with emptiness witnesses, DecisionClosure; crate names collide with ours (fa-reference, fa-policy, fa-verify, fa, fa-cli) so linking needs package renames; port invariants as fa-policy tests first). eidetic_engine_cli → fa-i8j design reference (daemon over a local Unix socket with 4-byte length-prefixed JSON frames and size limits, src/daemon/protocol.rs; title: Agent-safe authority on every surface: authenticated principals, issued capabilities, Agent-profile defaults, read-path authorization (reality check 2026-10-11)
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-11 at origin/staging e606b46): the plan's agent-safety story (§14.2 caveats, §14.4 profiles, doctrine 7 "SoD enforced at commit", doctrine 8 "authorization precedes observation", AGENTS.md "Do not write to trunk from an Agent-profile capability") is implemented correctly INSIDE the kernel (fa-policy admit/SoD, FA-REF-013 Agent-on-trunk, revocation witnesses) but every surface constructs the capability it presents from caller-supplied argv. `Capability::embedded(holder, op_names)` (crates/fa-policy/src/capability.rs:237-247) self-issues a Human-profile capability; fa-cli reads the principal from `--as` (crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:1476-1478) and ops from `--grant` (cli.rs:2104-2106, :2591-2595); fad forwards the client's argv unchanged into `cli::run` (crates/fad/src/lib.rs:194-216); fa-mcp exposes `as`, `grant`, `yes` and `keys` as tool arguments and turns them into argv (crates/fa-mcp/src/registry.rs:1381-1388; its own unit test at :1775-1800 pins `grant: post_closed, yes: true` → `--grant post_closed --yes`). Consequences, all verified in source: an MCP agent can act as any principal, grant itself post_closed/approve/migrate/witness, approve its own proposal as a second invented principal, and is never issued an Agent-profile capability, so FA-REF-013 and the Agent profile never fire outside tests. The MCP self-approval mistake detector even tells the agent to retry "with `as` set to a different, admissible principal" (crates/fa-mcp/src/detect.rs:484-488) — coaching impersonation. `fa capabilities` claims "The daemon/MCP posture binds the capability from an authenticated session" (cli.rs:1225), which is false today. Reads take no capability at all (crates/fa/src/book.rs:1162-1212), and `Book::read_document` returns privileged bytes without one (book.rs:982).

This epic makes the authority model real on the postures agents actually use (fad, fa-mcp), keeps the embedded owner posture explicit and labelled, and adds the adversarial tests that prove it. It does NOT weaken any kernel check; the kernel already does the right thing given an honest capability.

Children: fa-23r (MCP containment, ship first), fa-v62 (journaled issuance + holder-bound tokens + profiles registry), fa-r3q (fad session binding), fa-0x0 (read-path authorization), fa-087 (ungated privileged read), fa-vwf (intake authorization + derived provenance grade), fa-7dw (AccessEvent), fa-kae (signed approvals/attestations), fa-ohe (agent-safety red-team acceptance suite). Related existing beads: fa-llx (caveats in the kernel), fa-1d6 (revocation surface), fa-s30 (permit model), fa-t6m (current-policy spec), fa-kuu (redaction caveat), fa-s7x (drafts: the only legal place for Agent-profile writes).

Epic acceptance: fa-ohe's suite green on the exact landing tree; `fa capabilities --json` reports the binding posture truthfully; no surface accepts a principal or op from an untrusted caller.

title: Reversal effective date must fall in the target's period or later, and only registered classes may target a special period (Adjustment/Closing/Opening) — enforced in the kernel and independently in the oracle
description:
WHY (verified at e606b46): plan §8.1 "Reversal: exact negation of one target entry, same or later period"; §7.3 "only Adjusting, Closing, Elimination, Revision, Restatement, and Migration classes may target a special period, and a Normal target is the default". (a) The reversal path (crates/fa-journal/src/post.rs:1218-1399) checks target existence, exact side-swap and reversed-once but not that the reversal's effective date/period is ≥ the target's; the oracle has the same omission (crates/fa-reference/src/lib.rs:1766-1795), so the differential cannot catch it — a reversal can be back-dated into an earlier period than the fact it reverses. (b) Period resolution accepts `effective_period` naming a live Adjustment/Closing/Opening period for any admitted class (crates/fa-time/src/period.rs:208-216; no class check in post.rs:617-638), so an Original can be routed into adjustment period 13.

WHAT: (1) registry: add a `special_period_classes` table (or `[[kind]]` class rows) in registries/admissibility.toml naming exactly the classes allowed per special kind; kernel and oracle both derive from it (oracle via its own reader, fa-vfu). (2) kernel: after resolving the target (point witness on the target entry), resolve both periods in the calendar's order and refuse a reversal whose period precedes the target's (new FA-REF code, catalog row with fix "post the reversal in <target period> or a later open period"); refuse special-period targeting by unlisted classes (FA-REF-010 family). (3) oracle: independent implementation of both rules.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: same-period and later-period reversals commit; Adjusting into P13 commits; [ ] planted negatives: reversal dated one period before its target → refused; Original with effective_period = P13 → refused; [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-03, FA-INV-08) + differential + exhaustive class × kind test generated from the registry; [ ] consumers: fa-oz3, fa-4o0 (close), fa-xwv; [ ] no-claim boundary: period ordering per the book's calendar order, not civil-date order alone (P12 vs P13 share dates).

TESTS: genesis.rs negatives; fa-registry exhaustive table test; differential with seeds.

title: fa-conformance substrate behavior suite (plan §16.3): one test per relied-upon FrankenGraphDB behavior, run on every franken-stack.lock bump — the executable form of Appendix H's drift check
description:
WHY: plan §16.3: "The substrate behavior suite (fa-conformance/substrate/): one test per relied-upon substrate behavior — a point-read witness conflicts with a concurrent property write in both orders; SnapshotAdvanced then refresh_snapshot; delta_since is gap-free and DeltaCursorRetired triggers a rebuild; create_vertex refuses AlreadyLive; execute_certified then replay is byte-identical; open_memory parity with a directory book; write_ordered is one publication under finish_with_crash at every CrashPoint; … post-vs-close in both orders, an entry into an empty period (the witness is the Period vertex, not a scan), concurrent double application of one receipt, a limited-account race through the LimitCell CAS. It runs on every franken-stack.lock bump". At e606b46 there is no fa-conformance crate and no bead; the kernel relies on these behaviors (witness conflicts, AlreadyLive identities, delta_since) but they are exercised only incidentally, and the single-&mut-writer posting path means in-process tests never hit a first-committer-wins conflict (Folio audit). Memory of the swarm records one such substrate fact learned the hard way (a stale WriteTxn is refused at staging with SnapshotAdvanced, not at commit).

WHAT: crates/fa-conformance (verification layer; dev-only), substrate/ module with one test per behavior above using the substrate API directly (not the kernel), each asserting the exact typed outcome; a second group drives the kernel's two-transaction interleavings through prepare/commit to prove the witness design for post-vs-close in both orders (complements fa-0fl's DPOR); a check.sh step that runs the suite whenever franken-stack.lock or Cargo.lock changes; Appendix H rows gain a `conformance_test` column checked by fa-registry.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: suite green at the pinned rev; [ ] planted negatives: each test's expected outcome inverted in a mutation run fails exactly that test; [ ] proof class: conformance (bounded behavioral) ; [ ] consumers: every pin bump, fa-0fl, fa-c23; [ ] no-claim boundary: proves the behaviors at the pinned rev only.

TESTS: the suite with per-test logging of substrate outcomes.
